headline: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU LAUNCHES VARIOUS INITIATIVES AT RASHTRAPATI BHAVAN TO MARK THE COMPLETION OF FOUR YEARS OF HER PRESIDENCY
fullText:
President's Secretariat

PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU LAUNCHES VARIOUS INITIATIVES AT RASHTRAPATI BHAVAN TO MARK THE COMPLETION OF FOUR YEARS OF HER PRESIDENCY

28 JUL 2026 10:07PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu completed four years in the Office on July 25, 2026. To mark this occasion, the President graced the inauguration and laying of foundation stones for various important initiatives undertaken in Rashtrapati Bhavan and the President’s Estates today (July 28, 2026).

• Launch of e-Audio Guide for visitors to Rashtrapati Bhavan to enhance visitors' experience. The application-based e-Audio Guide will be available in Hindi, English and 14 other Indian languages. Its sign language module will also be available for visitors.

• Launch of the third edition of e-Upahaar, featuring 300 curated Presidential gifts for public auction. The auction will be open from 5 August to 5 September 2026 (more details at upahaar.rashtrapatibhavan.gov.in)

• Inauguration of Bachpan 'Bal Parisar' for the children in the President’s Estate. The initiative includes 'Kilkari', a play zone for children, and 'Samarth Anganwadi-cum-Palna', which provides a safe and nurturing environment for their growth and development.

• Launch of RAAHI (Rashtrapati Bhavan Access And Heritage Interconnector), a fare-free electric bus service to promote green and inclusive mobility. This bus service for the staff and residents of the President's Estate is being operated by women drivers and conductors. This will provide safe, convenient and inclusive mobility, particularly for women, children, senior citizens and Divyang persons within the President’s Estate and up to the nearest Metro station.

• Laying of foundation stone for the construction of service block as part of Net Zero Energy Strategy

• Inauguration of accommodation facilities at Rashtrapati Niketan, Dehradun and Rashtrapati Nilayam, Secunderabad as well as laying of foundation stone for the redevelopment of staff quarters in the President’s Estate.

Speaking on the occasion of launch of various initiatives, the President said that it has been a constant endeavour to ensure that Rashtrapati Bhavan stands as a vibrant symbol of India's rich traditions, democratic values, and national ideals. In the last one year, various steps were taken to promote India’s civilizational ethos, which include unveiling of the bust of Chakravarti Rajagopalachari Ji, inauguration of Param Vir Dirgha and Granth Kutir, Indianization of State Rooms and highlighting the Indian art and traditions in State Receptions.

Later in a separate function at Rashtrapati Bhavan, the Vice President of India, Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan, released publications pertaining to the Presidency of Smt Droupadi Murmu and presented their first copies to the President in presence of Dr L. Murugan, Minister of State for Information & Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs and other dignitaries.

The publications which were released today are - Rashtrapati Bhavan: Rashtra Ka Bhavan (President Droupadi Murmu's first year of Presidency); Seva Aur Samvedana (President Droupadi Murmu's second year of Presidency); Samaveshi Sahbhaghita (President Droupadi Murmu's third year of Presidency); Bharatiyata Ka Utsav (President Droupadi Murmu's fourth year of Presidency); and Ama Rashtrapati - Ama Gourav, a collection of articles in Odia, written by eminent persons.

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that the titles of these books reflect our faith in inclusive democracy. She expressed confidence that these illustrated compilations will introduce readers to the traditions, functioning and multiple facets of Rashtrapati Bhavan. She stated that their true significance lies in their ability to inspire fellow citizens to move forward on the path of progress while taking pride in their heritage.

The President said that when she assumed the office of the President of India on July 25, 2022, it was a matter of responsibility for her, even more than an honour. She stated that over the past four years, she had discharged her duties with this very sense of obligation. She said that whenever she meets people—especially the youth— at Rashtrapati Bhavan or during her visits to various states, she encourages them to remain rooted in ethical values and to work towards the progress of the nation and society. She said that she urges women to become self-reliant and to move forward on the path of progress with self-confidence. When interacting with members of tribal communities, she requests them to preserve their cultural heritage while also joining the mainstream of development. Whenever she travels abroad, she meets the Indian community in those countries and encourages them to contribute to India's journey of development.

In his remarks, the Vice President said that during the past four years, President Droupadi Murmu has enriched the high office with grace, humility, wisdom and commitment to the letter and spirit of the Constitution. Her remarkable life journey is extraordinary and deeply inspiring. Her rise from the modest surroundings of a remote tribal village in Odisha to the highest constitutional office of our great nation, is a testimony to the strength and inclusiveness of Indian democracy. He said that during his tenure as Governor of Jharkhand, the people he met across the state remembered her tenure as Governor with great warmth and admiration.

Highlighting key initiatives during President Droupadi Murmu’s Presidency, the Vice-President referred to Amrit Udyan, the opening of Rashtrapati Niketan and Rashtrapati Tapovan to the public, a more Divyangjan-friendly Rashtrapati Bhavan, and the installation of the bust of Chakravarti Rajagopalachari at Rashtrapati Bhavan. He said these initiatives reflected the vision of bringing the Presidency closer to the people while shedding the colonial mindset.

Recalling the release of the Constitution of India in the Santhali language in the Ol Chiki script, the Vice-President described it as a landmark initiative that filled the tribal community with pride and reaffirmed the nation’s commitment to preserving India’s linguistic and cultural heritage. He expressed confidence that books released today will help in preserving values that have defined the four years — constitutionality, service, compassion, inclusivity, cultural confidence and national unity.

headline: Sarbananda Sonowal Reviews Safety Preparedness for Indian Seafarers Amid Evolving Geopolitical Situation
fullText:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

Sarbananda Sonowal Reviews Safety Preparedness for Indian Seafarers Amid Evolving Geopolitical Situation

24×7 Support System in place to assist Indian Seafarers in conflict-affected regions

Indian Missions Across West Asia and Black Sea Join Centre's Seafarer Safety Review

28 JUL 2026 9:43PM by PIB Delhi

NEW DELHI, July 28, 2026: As geopolitical tensions continue to impact key global shipping routes, Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal, today undertook a comprehensive review of the safety and welfare of Indian seafarers serving aboard merchant vessels in conflict-sensitive regions, reaffirming the Government's commitment to ensuring that every Indian mariner remains safe, informed and supported.

The review brought together senior officials from the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), the Directorate General of Shipping (DGS), and Heads of Indian Missions from countries across West Asia and the Black Sea region, including Oman, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Russia and Ukraine. The Minister was briefed on the prevailing security situation, maritime developments and the preparedness of Indian diplomatic missions to respond swiftly to any contingency involving Indian seafarers.

During the meeting, Sarbananda Sonowal directed officials to maintain constant coordination across all agencies and emphasised that the safety of Indian seafarers must remain the Government's foremost priority. "No Indian seafarer should find himself caught in the crossfire of geopolitical conflict. Every possible measure must be taken to safeguard our seafarers, support their families and ensure timely assistance wherever required," Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said.

The Directorate General of Shipping further informed the Minister that its 24×7 Seafarer Grievance and Assistance Cell is fully operational, providing round-the-clock support to Indian seafarers and their families through dedicated helplines, information services and grievance redressal mechanisms.

To strengthen preparedness before deployment, the Minister also reviewed initiatives to enhance awareness among seafarers. The Recruitment and Placement Service Licensees (RPSLs) are being engaged to conduct structured pre-departure orientation programmes, enabling seafarers to better understand operational conditions, security protocols and evolving geopolitical risks in areas where they may be deployed.

Recognising the psychological impact of prolonged deployments in volatile regions, Sonowal directed that mental health support be integrated into India's seafarer welfare framework. He called for structured counselling services for both seafarers and their families and stressed that transparent communication on operational risks must become an essential part of pre-deployment preparation.

"Our responsibility extends beyond ensuring physical safety. Seafarers and their families deserve timely information, emotional support and complete transparency regarding the challenges they may face while serving at sea. We must strengthen every aspect of our welfare ecosystem to stand firmly with our maritime community during these uncertain times," Sonowal said.

The Minister also directed officials to maintain close coordination with Indian Missions abroad, shipping companies, maritime authorities and all relevant stakeholders so that India's response mechanism remains proactive, integrated and capable of responding swiftly.

(Release ID: 2290817)
summaryText:
### OVERVIEW  
The Indian government, led by Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal, convened a review to enhance safety and welfare measures for Indian seafarers amid escalating geopolitical tensions impacting global shipping routes, emphasizing increased support systems and pre-deployment preparedness.  

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS  
- Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal reviewed safety preparedness for Indian seafarers in conflict-sensitive regions during a meeting on July 28, 2026.  
- The review involved officials from the Ministry of External Affairs, Directorate General of Shipping, and Indian Missions in West Asia (Oman, Saudi Arabia, Iran) and the Black Sea (Russia, Ukraine).  
- A 24×7 Seafarer Grievance and Assistance Cell is operational, offering round-the-clock helplines, information, and grievance redressal.  
- Pre-departure orientation programs by Recruitment and Placement Service Licensees (RPSLs) were mandated to educate seafarers on security protocols and geopolitical risks.  
- Mental health support was proposed for seafarers and families, including structured counseling services to address psychological impacts of volatile deployments.  
- Emphasis on transparent communication of operational risks and enhanced coordination among maritime authorities, shipping companies, and diplomatic missions to ensure swift response capabilities.

headline: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah virtually inaugurates the newly constructed ‘Sahakar Bhavan’ of Jamnagar District Cooperative Bank
fullText:
Ministry of Cooperation

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah virtually inaugurates the newly constructed ‘Sahakar Bhavan’ of Jamnagar District Cooperative Bank

Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Ministry of Cooperation has infused new energy and momentum into the cooperative movement—Shri Amit Shah

Built with modern technology and in conformity with RBI and NABARD standards, ‘Sahakar Bhavan’ will play an important role in meeting the financial needs of farmers in Jamnagar and Devbhumi Dwarka

Constructed at a cost of approximately ₹25 crore, the building offers several state-of-the-art facilities, including a training centre, farmers’ hostel, modern conference halls and secure lockers

Deposits of ₹135 crore, loan disbursement of ₹780 crore, profit of ₹24 crore and zero NPA are major achievements of Jamnagar District Cooperative Bank—Shri Amit Shah

With 40 branches, 431 service cooperative societies and 652 milk producers’ societies, the bank will strengthen cooperation across villages

Over two lakh new PACS and dairy cooperative societies, along with more than 20 new business activities for PACS, will lay the foundation for rural prosperity—Shri Amit Shah

28 JUL 2026 9:39PM by PIB Delhi

Taking forward Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar Se Samriddhi’ and under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, another important step was taken today towards making the country’s cooperative banking system modern, transparent and farmer-centric. Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah virtually inaugurated ‘Sahakar Bhavan’, the newly constructed headquarters of Jamnagar District Cooperative Bank in Jamnagar, Gujarat. Equipped with state-of-the-art technology, the new headquarters will cater to the financial and institutional requirements of farmers, service cooperative societies and dairy cooperative institutions in the districts of Jamnagar and Devbhumi Dwarka.

Gujarat Chief Minister Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel, Cooperation Minister of Gujarat Shri Jitubhai Vaghani, Gujarat Cabinet Ministers Shri Arjunbhai Modhwadia, Shri Raghavjibhai Patel, Shri Mulubhai Bera, Member of Parliament from Jamnagar Smt. Poonamben Maadam, Minister of State and MLA from Jamnagar North Smt. Rivaba Jadeja, Chairman of Gujarat State Cooperative Bank Shri Ajaybhai Patel, and Chairman of Jamnagar District Cooperative Bank Shri Jitubhai Lal attended the programme or joined it virtually. Directors of Jamnagar District Cooperative Bank, senior officials of the district administration, chairpersons of Agricultural Produce Market Committees and district cooperative unions, office-bearers of the Jamnagar Milk Union, chairpersons of cooperative urban banks, representatives of service cooperative societies, several public representatives and a large number of farmers also participated in the programme.

Addressing the programme, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah congratulated the Chairman of Jamnagar District Cooperative Bank, all its directors, office-bearers of service cooperative societies and farmers on the construction of the new headquarters. He said that modernisation is essential for strengthening the cooperative system and that this process begins with modernising the headquarters and functioning of cooperative institutions.

Shri Amit Shah said the new headquarters of Jamnagar District Cooperative Bank has been constructed in conformity with all the standards prescribed by the Reserve Bank of India and NABARD and is equipped with state-of-the-art technology. He said the headquarters will help provide better, safer and more modern banking services to farmers, service cooperative societies and other cooperative institutions in Jamnagar district.

The Union Minister of Cooperation said that Jamnagar District Cooperative Bank, which began in 1969 with a modest capital of only ₹2.5 lakh, today has a business of more than ₹215 crore. He said that as service cooperative societies and dairy cooperative societies expand their areas of operation, the bank will play an increasingly important role as a major institution meeting the financial requirements of the cooperative sector across the district.

Shri Amit Shah said the modern headquarters, constructed at a cost of approximately ₹25 crore, has been built on 25,000 square feet of land and offers nearly 47,000 square feet of functional space. The building has been designed keeping in view the bank’s projected requirements for the next 15 years. The building has several facilities, including a training centre, farmers’ hostel, modern conference rooms, meeting halls, secure locker facilities and dining arrangements. He said the building will function as an energy centre for farmers in both Jamnagar and Devbhumi Dwarka districts. The installation of a 200-kilowatt solar power plant in the building is an important step towards developing it as a green building.

The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said the bank has total deposits of approximately ₹135 crore. It has disbursed loans amounting to ₹780 crore, earned a profit of ₹24 crore and has zero gross NPA. He described these achievements as evidence of the bank’s efficient management and commitment to cooperative values.

Shri Amit Shah said that the bank, which operates through 40 branches, will use the new headquarters to expand its reach to villages across Jamnagar district. The bank is associated with 431 service cooperative societies, six dairy unions and 652 milk producers’ societies and provides services to more than 1.5 lakh cooperative members.

The Union Minister of Cooperation said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India established a separate Ministry of Cooperation and infused new energy and momentum into the country’s cooperative movement. He said that initiatives such as establishing more than two lakh new Primary Agricultural Credit Societies and dairy cooperative societies, adding more than 20 new business activities to PACS, taking the audit system of cooperative institutions online and connecting different cooperative institutions with one another will play an important role in ensuring the prosperity of farmers and strengthening the rural economy in the coming years.

Shri Amit Shah said that during a future visit to Jamnagar, he would visit the new headquarters of Jamnagar District Cooperative Bank. He also said that during his visit, he would hold a meeting with representatives of the district’s service cooperative societies and dairy cooperative societies and discuss in detail issues relating to the expansion of the cooperative sector and the prosperity of farmers. He expressed confidence that Jamnagar District Cooperative Bank would grow stronger in the coming years and provide better services to citizens, farmers and cooperative institutions across villages.

headline: World Nature Conservation Day Celebrated at National Zoological Park, New Delhi
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

World Nature Conservation Day Celebrated at National Zoological Park, New Delhi

28 JUL 2026 9:17PM by PIB Delhi

The National Zoological Park, New Delhi (Delhi Zoo), successfully celebrated World Nature Conservation Day on 28 July 2026 with a series of awareness and conservation activities aimed at promoting environmental responsibility and sustainable living. The theme of World Nature Conservation Day 2026 focused on the conservation of natural resources and biodiversity, reinforcing the need for collective action to protect the environment.

As part of the celebrations, around 35 sanitation workers of the National Zoological Park participated in a plastic removal drive across the zoo premises. During the drive, around 230 kg of plastic waste, including plastic bottles, straws and other single-use plastic items, was collected, highlighting the zoo's continued commitment to maintaining a clean and environmentally sustainable campus.

The programme commenced with an interactive awareness session for zoo visitors on the objectives of the LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) initiative. The session focused on the themes of "Segregation of Waste" and "Waste to Useful Products", emphasising the importance of proper waste management in reducing pollution and conserving natural resources.

To further engage visitors, a doodle activity was organised, in which participants enthusiastically expressed their ideas on nature conservation and sustainable lifestyles through creative artwork. The activities were designed to encourage visitors to adopt environmentally responsible practices and strengthen their connection with nature.

The celebration concluded with the distribution of prizes and souvenirs to the participating staff in recognition of their valuable contribution to the plastic removal drive and the successful conduct of the programme. Through such initiatives, the National Zoological Park continues to promote environmental awareness and inspire visitors to embrace sustainable practices for the conservation of nature and biodiversity.

(Release ID: 2290799)

headline: CAQM reviews progress of Special Campaign for Removal of Legacy Dust across 12 MCD Zones; Directs Sustained Dust Mitigation Efforts
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

CAQM reviews progress of Special Campaign for Removal of Legacy Dust across 12 MCD Zones; Directs Sustained Dust Mitigation Efforts

28 JUL 2026 8:55PM by PIB Delhi

The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) today reviewed the progress of the Special Campaign for Removal of Legacy Dust being undertaken across all 12 Zones of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD). The Commission directed that the campaign should continue as a sustained and phased exercise with periodic repetition, continuous monitoring and regular maintenance, rather than as a one-time initiative. It also emphasised the need to strengthen inter-agency coordination, address identified gaps in a time-bound manner and intensify dust mitigation measures for effective control of air pollution in Delhi.

The review meeting was held under the Chairmanship of Shri Tarun Kumar Pithode, Member Secretary, CAQM. Deputy Commissioners (DCs)/representatives of all the MCD Zones presented the status of implementation, achievements, challenges encountered and the way forward. The meeting formed part of the follow-up mechanism pursuant to the CAQM letter issued on 11.05.2026. It directed Dust Control and Management Cells (DCMCs) in Delhi to undertake a special campaign for identification, removal and scientific disposal of legacy dust from roads, roadsides, medians, footpaths and other associated areas under their jurisdiction.

The Commission reviewed the dust mitigation measures undertaken by all MCD Zones, including mechanized road sweeping, manual cleaning, water sprinkling, removal of accumulated dust and debris, deployment of sanitation workers and close on-ground monitoring. The zone-wise progress is as follows:

S. No. | MCD Zone | Duration of dust removal | Total Road Length Covered (in Kilometres) | Legacy Dust / Waste Removed (in Metric Tonne)

1. | Rohini Zone | 01.01.2026 – 26.07.2026 | 24,486 kms. | 2,950.40 MT

2. | Outer North Zone | 01.03.2026 – 28.07.2026 | 8,057 kms. | 948.66 MT

3. | Najafgarh Zone | 05.06.2026 – 25.07.2026 | 24.5 kms. | 270 MT

4. | Keshav Puram Zone | 18.05.2026 – 29.05.2026 | 117.5 kms. | 218 MT

5. | Civil Lines Zone | 01.05.2026 – 26.07.2026 | 128 kms. | 95.65 MT

6. | Old Delhi Zone | 18.05.2026 – 27.07.2026 | 179.4 kms. | 386.4 MT

7. | Karol Bagh Zone | 18.05.2026 – 27.06.2026 | 122 kms. | 378 MT

8. | Central Zone | 12.05.2026 – 28.07.2026 | 240 kms./ day | 12.8 MT/ day

9. | West Zone | 01.06.2026 – 28.07.2026 | 10,137.5 kms. | 638.5 MT

10. | Shahdara South Zone | 01.05.2026 – 26.07.2026 | 150 kms. | 135.89 MT

11. | Shahdara North Zone | 06.06.2026 – 28.07.2026 | 81.7 kms. | 906.8 MT

12. | South Zone | 01.06.2026 – 30.06.2026 | 05 kms./ day | 623.49 MT

The DCs/representatives highlighted several operational challenges during the campaign. They included the limited utility of Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines (MRSMs) on roads less than nine metres wide due to parked vehicles. Further, overflow of water during irrigation of central verges by other agencies led to repeated deposition of soil and dust on carriageways, absence of end-to-end paving on several road stretches resulted in recurring dust generation, and continued littering despite the availability of adequate waste bins.

The need for sustained Information, Education and Communication (IEC) initiatives to promote behavioural change among citizens was also emphasised. The Commission advised that IEC activities should be intensified to promote citizen participation and responsibility. It also called for regular capacity-building and training workshops for sanitation workers to enhance operational efficiency, in accordance with the Framework for targeted IEC activities by NCR States and GNCTD for abatement of air pollution, issued by CAQM on 03.03.2026.

CAQM further emphasised that all concerned agencies should prioritise end-to-end paving and greening of roads in accordance with the Standard Framework issued by the Commission on 07.01.2025, to eliminate exposed soil and prevent recurring dust generation. It also stressed the need for plantation and landscaping using suitable soil-trapping plant species to minimise soil erosion and reduce dust re-suspension instead of excessive concretisation of open areas.

(Release ID: 2290780)

### OVERVIEW
The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) reviewed the progress of the Special Campaign for Removal of Legacy Dust across all 12 Zones of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) and directed that the campaign continue as a sustained, phased exercise with continuous monitoring and regular maintenance.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- **Review Date**: 28 July 2026
- **Campaign Scope**: Implementation across all 12 MCD Zones under the CAQM directive dated 11.05.2026
- **Total Road Length Covered**: 36,987.1 km (cumulative across all zones)

  - Conduct regular capacity-building and training workshops for sanitation workers

  - Limited effectiveness of Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines (MRSMs) on narrow roads with parked vehicles
  - Repeated dust deposition due to water overflow from irrigation activities
  - Recurring dust generation from unpaved road stretches
  - Continued littering despite adequate waste bin availability
- **Chairman**: Shri Tarun Kumar Pithode, Member Secretary, CAQM
- **Follow-up Reference**: Based on CAQM Framework for IEC activities issued on 03.03.2026 and Standard Framework issued on 07.01.2025

headline: PM Chairs Second High-Level Meeting with Secretaries of Government of India
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

PM Chairs Second High-Level Meeting with Secretaries of Government of India

Sectors discussed: Finance and Economy, Commerce and Industry, and Technology

PM emphasises the need to break both horizontal and vertical silos within the Government

PM emphasises the importance of technological self-reliance and building domestic capabilities in critical sectors

PM encourages greater participation of young innovators and entrepreneurs in cybersecurity ecosystem

PM Stresses Proactive Outreach on Strategic Sectors to Counter Misinformation

PM says Govt must always remain youthful, dynamic and forward-looking, continuously adapting to new challenges and opportunities with agility and innovation

Secretaries share experiences and perspectives on key initiatives, emerging opportunities and implementation challenges

28 JUL 2026 8:48PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the second high-level meeting with Secretaries to the Government of India at his residence at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg earlier today. He reviewed the future action agenda of Ministries and Departments dealing with Finance and Economy, Commerce and Industry, and Technology sectors. The meeting focused on accelerating progress towards the goals of Viksit Bharat.

Prime Minister called for a strong focus on team building across Ministries and Departments, urging officers to work with a shared sense of purpose. He emphasised the need to break both horizontal and vertical silos within the Government so that departments function in close coordination and deliver integrated outcomes.

Highlighting the importance of citizen-centric governance, Prime Minister said that the people of India must remain at the centre of governance. He reminded that every decision and policy should be guided by the interests and aspirations of the common citizen.

Prime Minister stressed that while India is making significant investments in infrastructure, equal priority must be given to developing indigenous technologies. He underscored the importance of technological self-reliance and building domestic capabilities in critical sectors.

Prime Minister underlined that energy security is closely linked with national security, economic stability and citizens’ welfare. Prime Minister said India must achieve self-reliance in the energy sector through innovation, diversification and accelerated capacity creation.

Emphasising that reforms are not merely a fashionable term but a continuous necessity for effective governance, Prime Minister stressed the need to reform processes, improve work culture and strengthen institutional efficiency.

Prime Minister said that growing use of technology must be accompanied by a strong focus on cybersecurity to safeguard digital systems and infrastructure. He stressed the need for constant vigilance against emerging cyber threats. He called for encouraging greater participation of young innovators and entrepreneurs in the cybersecurity ecosystem and emphasised that it should evolve into a nationwide movement.

Prime Minister also emphasised the importance of proactive communication on strategic sectors where the country is undertaking major initiatives, to counter misinformation and unfounded fears surrounding such efforts.

fullText:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting

President Droupadi Murmu's Four Years in Office Marked by Release of Five Commemorative Books at Rashtrapati Bhavan

Commemorative Books Reflect Nation's Faith in Inclusive Democracy and Inspire Citizens to Take Pride in India's Heritage: Smt. Droupadi Murmu

President Murmu has Enriched the Highest Constitutional Office with Grace, Humility, Wisdom and Unwavering Commitment to the Constitution: Vice-President

28 JUL 2026 8:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today released and presented the first set of five commemorative books, marking four years of the Presidency of the Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, to the President at Rashtrapati Bhavan.

On completion of four years of the Presidency of Hon’ble President Smt. Droupdi Murmu, four books, Rashtrapati Bhavan: Rashtra Ka Bhavan, Seva aur Samvedana, Samaveshi Sahbhagita and Bharatiyata Ka Utsav, were released today at Rashtrapati Bhavan. These books are published by the Publications Division, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Besides these books, another book in odia, Ama Rastrapati Ama Gourav, was also released. Ama Rastrapati Ama Gourav is a collection of articles on the Hon’ble President of India.

President Droupadi Murmu received first copies of publications on her Presidency from Vice President of India Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan who formally released these at a function held at Rashtrapati Bhavan. Dr L. Murugan, Minister of State for Information & Broadcasting and… pic.twitter.com/efvYFj0Sh3

— President of India (@rashtrapatibhvn) July 28, 2026

The books were released in the august presence of the Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, Hon’ble Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, and Hon’ble Union Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan.

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that the titles of these books reflect our faith in inclusive democracy. She expressed confidence that these illustrated compilations will introduce readers to the traditions, functioning and multiple facets of Rashtrapati Bhavan. She stated that their true significance lies in their ability to inspire fellow citizens to move forward on the path of progress while taking pride in their heritage.

The President said that when she assumed the office of the President of India on July 25, 2022, it was a matter of responsibility for her, even more than an honour. She stated that over the past four years, she had discharged her duties with this very sense of obligation. She said that whenever she meets people, especially the youth, at Rashtrapati Bhavan or during her visits to various States, she encourages them to remain rooted in ethical values and to work towards the progress of the nation and society. She said that she urges women to become self-reliant and to move forward on the path of progress with self-confidence. When interacting with members of tribal communities, she requests them to preserve their cultural heritage while also joining the mainstream of development. Whenever she travels abroad, she meets the Indian community in those countries and encourages them to contribute to India's journey of development.

Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that the occasion held special personal significance for him, recalling his tenure as Governor of Jharkhand. He noted that during his extensive travels across the State, people from all walks of life spoke with great warmth and admiration about Smt. Droupadi Murmu’s tenure as Governor. He observed that citizens fondly remembered the dignity with which she discharged her constitutional responsibilities, her deep personal connect with the people, and her empathy and genuine concern for tribal communities, the underprivileged and the youth. “Such goodwill cannot be earned by office alone, it is earned through character, compassion and dedication to the people,” he said.

Highlighting several initiatives undertaken during President Murmu’s tenure, the Vice-President referred to the renaming of the historic Mughal Gardens as Amrit Udyan, the opening of Rashtrapati Niketan and Rashtrapati Tapovan in Dehradun to the public, efforts to make Rashtrapati Bhavan more Divyangjan-friendly, and the replacement of the bust of Sir Edwin Lutyens with that of Bharat Ratna Chakravarti Rajagopalachari, the last Governor-General of India. He said these initiatives reflected a conscious effort to free national institutions from the colonial mindset while bringing the institution of the Presidency closer to the people.

Referring to the publications, Shri Radhakrishnan said Seva aur Samvedana highlights the values of service and empathy that have characterised President Murmu’s public life, while Samaveshi Sahbhagita reflects her conviction that India’s development must be inclusive and participatory. He said Bharatiyata Ka Utsav celebrates the timeless values of India’s civilisation and its remarkable cultural diversity, adding that President Murmu has consistently highlighted India’s cultural richness, local traditions and spiritual heritage that unite the nation while celebrating its diversity.

Recalling the release of the Constitution of India in the Santhali language in the Ol Chiki script by the President, the Vice-President described it as a momentous occasion that filled members of the tribal community with pride and reaffirmed the nation’s commitment to preserving and promoting India’s linguistic and cultural diversity.

Union Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, was present at the launch of the books at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi. On the occasion, he said that the books capture the cultural diversity of the country. He said these books will play an important role as reference books for future generations. He added that the publications launched today mark an important milestone in documenting the Presidential journey of Hon’ble President Droupadi Murmu.

headline: Union Minister for Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia reviews progress of Bharat 6G Alliance, presents 5G Lab Excellence Awards
fullText:

Union Minister for Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia reviews progress of Bharat 6G Alliance, presents 5G Lab Excellence Awards

B6GA is working towards achieving Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s Vision of Making India a Front-Line Contributor in Telecom Technology

Bharat 6G Alliance Must Benchmark Global Progress and Strengthen Collaboration among Working Groups: Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia

28 JUL 2026 7:51PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia today reviewed the progress of the Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA) at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, along with Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development and Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary (Telecom).

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had released India’s 6G Vision “Bharat 6G Vision” document on March 22th, 2023 which envisages India to be a front-line contributor in design, development and deployment of 6G technology by 2030.

The meeting reviewed the progress and Action Taken by the Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA) towards advancing India’s 6G ambitions. The Alliance functions through seven specialised Working Groups covering Spectrum; Device Technology & Manufacturing Ecosystem; Technology; Applications; Green & Sustainability; Outreach; and 6G Use Cases & Revenue Streams.

The members organisations of the alliance collectively hold more than 7,700 patent filings related to 5G and 6G technologies, including 4,400+ foreign filings, reflecting the growing strength of India’s research and innovation ecosystem. India’s participation in the 3GPP has also increased significantly, with the number of Indian participants rising from 717 in 2020 to 1,787 in 2025, while technical contributions increased from 196 to 2,943 during the same period.

An update on 6G Technology Standardisation Efforts by the Telecom Standards Development Society, India (TSDSI) was also presented. The discussions highlighted the importance of India’s active and meaningful participation in global standardisation processes and the need to ensure that Indian innovations, technologies, use cases and requirements contribute to the development of globally relevant 6G standards.

Quarterly updates of the Bharat 6G Alliance Working Groups were presented during the meeting, covering six key areas of the 6G ecosystem—Technology; Applications & 6G Use Cases and Revenue Streams; Green and Sustainability; Spectrum; Devices Technology, Components, Sensors and Manufacturing Ecosystem; and Outreach. The deliberations focused on accelerating indigenous research and development, identifying emerging applications and use cases, strengthening spectrum strategies, promoting energy-efficient and sustainable technologies, developing domestic capabilities in devices, components, sensors and manufacturing, and expanding collaboration and outreach across the ecosystem.

The meeting emphasised the importance of building a robust end-to-end telecommunications ecosystem in India, with stronger linkages between research, innovation, standards, manufacturing and market deployment. The participants discussed the need for greater collaboration among Government, industry, academia, startups and research institutions to accelerate technology development, enable translation of research into deployable solutions and create globally competitive products and services.

The 5G Labs Excellence Awards, based on cumulative performance during January–June 2026, recognised outstanding performance in utilisation, engagement, innovation and overall excellence in 5G/5G-Advanced technologies were also presented during the event. The awards acknowledge institutions and stakeholders for their contribution to experimentation, innovation, testing, skill development and the development of applications and use cases based on 5G and 5G-Advanced technologies. Based on cumulative performance during the period January–June 2026, four award categories were instituted, namely:

Award Category | Rank 1 | Rank 2 | Rank 3

5G Lab Excellence Award | IIITDM Kurnool | DKTE Textile & Engineering Institute, Maharashtra | IIT Roorkee

5G Lab Utilisation Excellence Award | IIITDM Kurnool | IIT Ropar | PEC Chandigarh

5G Lab Engagement Excellence Award | IIITDM Kurnool | IIT Roorkee | THDC Institute of Hydropower Engineering & Technology, Tehri

5G Lab Innovation Excellence Award | IIITDM Kurnool | DKTE Textile & Engineering Institute, Maharashtra | IIIT Delhi

IIITDM Kurnool secured the first position in all four categories, reflecting its outstanding overall performance among 5G Use Case Labs across the country.

An Open Discussion and Interaction with participants was held providing an opportunity for stakeholders to share their perspectives on emerging technologies, opportunities and challenges in the 6G ecosystem. The interaction covered key issues including technology development, standardisation, spectrum, sustainable communications, devices and manufacturing, applications and use cases, as well as mechanisms for strengthening collaboration among various stakeholders.

In the key remark, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, reiterated the Government’s commitment to positioning India as a leading contributor to the global telecommunications ecosystem. He emphasised that India’s 6G journey must be anchored in indigenous research and innovation, strong standards participation, domestic manufacturing, sustainable technologies and global partnerships. Shri Scindia said, “There has been a tremendous amount of progress since the last meeting. I would like to congratulate the team on accomplishing set targets and look forward to achieving next set of objectives in a dynamic manner. We should see where all other international grouping are in their progress of achieving 6G and how we compare to them. We should also identify areas of intersections amongst the working groups and how there can be scope of collaborations amongst them.”

The Union Minister suggested to focus on identifying areas of intersection among the seven working groups to foster greater synergy and collaboration, while benchmarking the country’s progress against international 6G groupings to identify gaps, learn from global best practices and further improve its performance. He also noted the participants’ suggestions for greater support from the Ministry and Government, alongside the need to foster a robust ecosystem encompassing academia, research and development, and world-class testing infrastructure to strengthen India’s capabilities in 6G technology.

The Union Minister further emphasised the importance of creating a secure, resilient, sustainable and inclusive telecommunications ecosystem capable of supporting India’s digital aspirations and contributing to global technological advancement. He noted that the convergence of research, innovation, standards, manufacturing and applications will be critical to ensuring that India not only adopts next-generation technologies but also contributes significantly to their global development.

Delivering the Keynote Address, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development, emphasised the importance of innovation, research and development and close collaboration between Government, industry, academia and research institutions in building a future-ready telecommunications ecosystem. He highlighted the need to accelerate indigenous technology development, nurture talent and create an enabling environment for startups and innovators to develop solutions for emerging communication technologies. Dr. Pemmasani said, “I am pleased to see the remarkable progress made by the Bharat 6G Alliance in bringing together industry, academia, startups and research institutions to shape India's 6G future. The collective efforts of its stakeholders and working groups have laid a strong foundation for innovation, indigenous technology development and global standardisation. As we move forward, it is essential to further deepen collaboration across all stakeholders, strengthen coordination among the working groups, and accelerate research, testing and standards development.”

The Bharat 6G Alliance Review Meeting reaffirmed the collective resolve to accelerate India’s 6G journey through coordinated efforts across technology, applications and use cases, sustainability, spectrum, devices and manufacturing, standardisation and outreach. The discussions and interactions provided further momentum to the vision of developing an indigenous, globally interoperable and future-ready telecommunications ecosystem, enabling India to emerge as a significant global hub for 6G innovation, technology, standards and deployment.

About Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA)

The Bharat 6G Alliance is a multi-stakeholder collaborative platform bringing together academia, industry, startups and public institutions to build a world-class, future-ready 6G ecosystem in India. Focusing on R&D, innovation and standardisation, B6GA plays a pivotal role in advancing India’s vision of global leadership in next-generation communication technologies.

Assam Exports First International Consignment of Purabi Ice Cream to Bhutan

Chief Minister Dr Himanta Biswa Sarma Flags Off First Purabi Ice Cream Export Consignment to Bhutan

29 JUL 2026 2:01PM by PIB Delhi

Marking a significant milestone for Assam's dairy sector and the North Eastern Region's processed food exports, the first international consignment of 5,627 litres of Purabi Ice Cream was exported from Assam to Bhutan, opening new avenues for value-added dairy exports from the region.

The export consignment was flagged off by Chief Minister of Assam, Dr Himanta Biswa Sarma, in Guwahati on 28 July 2026. Exported by North East Dairy and Foods Limited (NEDFL), the shipment will supply Purabi Ice Cream to key markets across Bhutan, including Thimphu, Paro, Phuentsholing and Wangdue, strengthening the presence of dairy products from Assam and the North Eastern Region in neighbouring international markets.

Manufactured by the West Assam Milk Producers' Cooperative Union Limited (WAMUL) and marketed by North East Dairy and Foods Limited (NEDFL), Purabi Ice Cream is produced using milk procured through Purabi Dairy's extensive cooperative network of dairy farmers across Assam. The inaugural consignment comprises a diverse range of products, including cups, family packs, cones and gallon packs, catering to both retail consumers and institutional buyers in Bhutan.

The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), under the Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of India, has been consistently promoting exports of agricultural and processed food products from the North Eastern Region by facilitating exporters in meeting international standards and accessing overseas markets. The export reflects APEDA's continued efforts to promote value-added products from the region and expand their global market reach.

APEDA facilitated the shipment by extending support in export documentation, regulatory compliance, market access facilitation and stakeholder coordination, ensuring the seamless movement of the consignment to Bhutan while strengthening the export ecosystem for processed dairy products from the North Eastern Region.

Bhutan's geographical proximity provides a natural advantage for expanding dairy exports from Assam and serves as an important gateway for enhancing the presence of Made-in-Assam dairy products in neighbouring international markets. Going forward, NEDFL plans to diversify its export portfolio by introducing additional Purabi Dairy products with longer shelf life and progressively increasing export volumes in line with market demand.

The initiative is expected to strengthen the international presence of dairy products from the North Eastern Region, create sustainable export opportunities for the dairy industry, and enhance income prospects for thousands of dairy farmers associated with Assam's cooperative milk network.

APEDA continues to work closely with State Governments, exporters, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), cooperatives and other stakeholders to enhance the global competitiveness of India's agricultural and processed food products while creating sustainable export-led growth opportunities for farmers and agri-enterprises across the country.

Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs

Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs Organizes Youth Parliament Programme to Strengthen Democratic Awareness

29 JUL 2026 1:41PM by PIB Delhi

To strengthen democratic awareness and parliamentary education, the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs organizes the Youth Parliament Programme under three categories.

Competition-based Youth Parliament Programme - The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs organizes the following Youth Parliament Competitions for the students of schools, colleges, and universities in coordination with the respective stakeholder organizations:

Youth Parliament Competition for schools under the Directorate of Education of Govt. of NCT of Delhi and Department of Education, New Delhi Municipal Council;

National Youth Parliament Competition for Kendriya Vidyalayas;

National Youth Parliament Competition for Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas;

National Youth Parliament Competition for Universities/Colleges; and

National Youth Parliament Competition for Eklavya Model Residential Schools

Participation-based Youth Parliament Programme - The Ministry has introduced a web-portal of the National Youth Parliament Scheme (NYPS) to increase the outreach of the Youth Parliament programme of the Ministry to hitherto untouched sections and corners of the country. The programme is voluntary in nature and is open to all citizens across the country through NYPS 2.0, irrespective of gender, caste, creed, religion, race, region, or location. Participants may organize Youth Parliament Sittings under the Institution/Group Participation categories or attempt the online quiz under the Individual Participation category, as per the prescribed guidelines. After successful participation, certificates are generated through the NYPS Helpdesk. Till date approximately 1.7 lakh students/citizens have participated in the web portal-based NYPS.

Financial Assistance to States/Union Territories for organizing Youth Parliament Competitions- The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs also provides financial assistance to States/UTs for organizing Youth Parliament Competitions by reimbursing the actual expenditure incurred, subject to the submission of claims and the prescribed annual ceilings. The reimbursement ceiling is ₹3 lakh for Legislatures with up to 100 members, ₹4 lakh for Legislatures with 101–200 members, ₹5 lakh for Legislatures with more than 200 members, and ₹2 lakh for Union Territories without a Legislature.

The Ministry does not conduct orientation or training programmes for parliamentary awareness as a standalone activity. However, prior to the commencement of each Youth Parliament Competition mentioned at point (1), an Orientation Course is organised for Principals, Teachers-in-Charge, and Coordinators of participating institutions to familiarise them with the procedures and methodology for conducting a Youth Parliament Sitting. No financial assistance is provided to the participating institutions for attending these Orientation Courses. headline: PM Vidyalaxmi Scheme
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

PM Vidyalaxmi Scheme

Promoting Educational Inclusion in India

29 JUL 2026 1:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Pradhan Mantri Vidyalaxmi Scheme is a flagship initiative of the Education Ministry that seeks to make quality higher education accessible to deserving students facing financial constraints. The scheme provides collateral-free and guarantor-free education loans to such students for studying in top ranked higher education institutions in the country. It further supports beneficiaries through interest subvention based on family income, reducing financial constraints to educational attainment. In doing so, the scheme contributes to India's progress towards SDG 4, which seeks to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all by 2030.

Bridging Financial Barriers to Higher Education

India has witnessed rapid expansion in higher education enrolment over the last decade, with the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) rising from 23.7% in 2014-15 to 30.0%in 2023-24. However, for many meritorious students, access to quality higher education in the top-ranked institutions of the country often remains difficult due to financial constraints. Many try to fill the gaps through education loans, but there are many more who cannot afford the high interest rates on these loans. The dreams of these students to study in IITs, IIMs and many other top-ranked institutions of the country remain unfulfilled despite their merit. The PM Vidyalaxmi Scheme (PM-Vidyalaxmi), approved by the Union Cabinet on 6th November 2024, comes to the aid of such students. This is a mission-mode intervention under which collateral-free, guarantor-free education loans are provided to students who have got admission on their own merit to one of the designated Quality Higher Educational Institutions (QHEIs) in the country. A 3% interest subvention is also provided for students with annual family income up to ₹8,00,000. The entire process for getting these loans is simple, transparent, student-friendly and entirely digital. There is a unified portal through which students can apply for education loans, track the status of their applications, claim interest subvention and also raise grievances.

The scheme stems from the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020, which recommends that financial assistance should be made available to meritorious students through various measures for studies in both public and private Higher Education Institutions (HEIs). The objective is to ensure that lack of finance does not prevent any meritorious student from studying in the best institutions in the country. PM-Vidyalaxmi positively contributes to the goals of SDG 4 and NEP 2020by advancing inclusive and equitable quality education and promoting lifelong learning opportunities for all.

Features, Benefits and Coverage

PM-Vidyalaxmi provides collateral-free and guarantor-free education loans for students admitted on their own merit to designated QHEIs in the country. Currently, 1,425 QHEIs are covered under the scheme, including both public and private institutions. Management quota, NRI quota, etc. admissions will not get this benefit.

Loans up to ₹ 7.5 lakhs are provided 75% credit guarantee by Government of India, to support banks to expand coverage. For students with up to ₹ 8 lakhs annual family income, the scheme provides for 3% interest subvention on loans up to ₹ 10 lakh. This is in addition to the full interest subvention already offered to students with up to ₹ Rs. 4.5 lakhs annual family income.

Collateral-free, Guarantor-free Education Loans

Students admitted to eligible QHEIs can obtain education loans without furnishing collateral or third-party guarantees under PM-Vidyalaxmi. There is no cut-off on highest amount of education loan. It will depend on course fee and other fees charged by the QHEI and other associated expenses (like mess, hostel fee, other refundable and non-refundable fees of the QHEI, cost of a reasonable quality laptop and reasonable amount of living expenses required by the student during the course period) and students from all income categories are eligible to apply.

To encourage lending institutions to extend loans to students, the Government provides a 75% credit guarantee for loans up to ₹7.5 lakh. This significantly reduces lender risk and improves loan accessibility.

The interest rates charged on the educational loan under the scheme will be capped at the individual bank’s Externally Benchmarked Lending Rate (EBLR) + 0.5%. The rate will always be less than the interest rate charged by the bank on other education loans not covered under PM-Vidyalaxmi. The repayment period of the education loan is up to 15 years, excluding a moratorium period of the course period plus one year. The loan is available for all degree /diploma programmes in India and there is no limit on the number of students getting such loans. The educational loans are provided through Scheduled Banks, Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), and Cooperative Banks participating in the scheme.

Interest Subvention

PM-Vidyalaxmi supplements the PM-USP CSIS (Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme). Under PM-USP CSIS, students who are pursuing technical/ professional courses from approved NAAC accredited HEIs/ NBA accredited courses and whose annual family income is up to ₹4.5 lakhs, shall be eligible for 100% interest subvention during moratorium period for education loan up to ₹ 10 lakhs.

PM-Vidyalaxmi interest subvention scheme’s coverage is broad-based and includes all courses at designated Quality Higher Educational Institutions (QHEIs). Under the scheme, interest subvention of 3% on loans up to ₹ 10 lakhs is awarded during the moratorium period (course period plus one year) to those meritorious students whose family’s annual income is less than ₹8,00,000.

If the education loan amount is more than ₹ 10 lakhs, interest subvention is provided for the disbursed total principal amount of the loan up to ₹ 10 lakhs only.

Student availing any other Central /State Government Scholarship or any other interest subvention scheme or Fee reimbursement shall not be eligible for availing interest subvention benefits under CSIS or PM-Vidyalaxmi.

In a year, a maximum of one lakh students shall be eligible for 3% interest subvention during the moratorium period. No such limit is for CSIS beneficiaries.

Understanding Interest Subvention under PM-USP CSIS and PM-Vidyalaxmi – available on PM-Vidyalaxmi Portal:

Institutions | NAAC/ NBA accredited, INIs, technical institutes approved by regulatory bodies like Medical Commission of India, Nursing Council, Bar Council, Pharmacy Council, Dental Council | Top 100 in NIRF – Private State govt- top 200 in NIRF Remaining central govt

Course | Professional/ technical courses | All degree/diploma courses

Family income | ₹ 4.5 lakh | ₹ 8 lakh

Interest subvention | Full interest subvention during moratorium period | 3% interest subvention during moratorium period

No of slots | No limit | 1 lakh fresh slots per year

Loan repayment | Up to 15 years after moratorium period (course period + 1 year)

The scheme offers affordable education loans with interest rates capped at the bank's Externally Benchmarked Lending Rate (EBLR) + 0.5%. In addition, banks may provide up to 1% additional interest concession to the borrowers if the interest is serviced during the study and the moratorium period. The scheme also provides tax benefits on the interest paid under Section 80E.

Interest subvention and credit guarantee benefits are available only once for undergraduate, postgraduate, or integrated courses. The Government has allocated a budget of ₹ 3,600 Crores from 2024-2025 to 2030-2031 for the scheme. 7 lakh fresh students are expected to get the benefit of this interest subvention during the seven-year period.

Eligibility Criteria for Students

The scheme is available to students who have secured merit-based admission through competitive exams in any of the designated Quality Higher Education Institutions (QHEIs) in India.

The scheme provides education loans for all degree and diploma courses.

The repayment period of the education loan would be up to 15 years excluding the moratorium period (course period + 1 year).

To avail all these benefits, students are required to register through Aadhaar, remain enrolled in their courses, and maintain a satisfactory academic performance.

Additional Conditions:

The applicant must not discontinue the course midway or be expelled from the institution due to disciplinary or academic reasons.

From the second year onwards, the student must maintain satisfactory academic performance to continue receiving interest subvention benefits.

The student can avail of interest subvention and credit guarantee benefits only once, either for an undergraduate, postgraduate, or integrated course.

Eligibility Criteria for Higher Education Institutions

The criteria for shortlisting institutions are based on their NIRF rankings. It currently covers institutions that are

Top 100 ranked HEIs in the overall/ category-specific and/or domain-specific rankings in the latest list of NIRF published by the Ministry of Education

Top 200 ranked HEIs under the governance of State/Union Territories governments in the latest list of NIRF published by the Ministry of Education

All remaining HEIs under the governance of the Government of India.

Indian campuses of foreign education institutions, foreign campuses of Indian education institutions and foreign education institutions are not covered under the scheme.

The criteria to select HEIs across India ensures equitable inter-state representation.

This list is updated using the latest NIRF ranking. As of now, 1,425 institutions are covered under PM-Vidyalaxmi and are eligible for PM-Vidyalaxmi education loans.

Steps for Availing Benefits

PM-Vidyalaxmi aims to make higher education more accessible by providing students with easy access to educational loans through a user-friendly digital platform. The scheme simplifies the loan process by enabling students to apply online, track their applications, and receive timely approvals and disbursements.

The scheme operates through a dedicated scheme portal that enables:

Common loan applications

Tracking of application status

Interest subvention requests

Digital processing and transparency.

PM Vidyalaxmi Digital Rupee App (CBDC Wallet)

Once the loan is sanctioned and disbursed, eligible students can apply for interest subvention based on their family income. The subsidy amount is credited to the beneficiary's PM Vidyalaxmi Digital Rupee App (CBDC Wallet) and subsequently transferred to the education loan account.

Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme (CSIS) provides full interest subsidy during the moratorium period on loan availed for pursuing technical/professional courses in India. Students whose annual gross parental/ family income is up to ₹ 4.5 lakh are eligible under the scheme.

Existing PM-USP CSIS is being administered through the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal and PM-Vidyalaxmi Digital Rupee Wallet. As of July 22, 2026, there are 35,777 active wallets enabling disbursement of subsidies worth ₹57.66 crore. This digital mechanism has helped streamline benefit delivery, reduce delays, and ensure that financial support reaches eligible students efficiently. For FY 2025-26, total claims pertaining to 2024-25, received at Canara Bank are 414844 amounting to ₹ 892.81 crores, which will significantly reduce repayment burden of the student beneficiaries. The portal also provides students with a platform to raise and monitor grievances, ensuring transparency and timely resolution of disputes.

Impact of PM Vidyalaxmi Scheme

PM-Vidyalaxmi is designed as a unified, fully digital and transparent education loan facilitation platform, enabling students to apply to banks for all kinds of education loans including PM-Vidyalaxmi loans, through a single portal and track their application status online. The dashboard provides real-time statistics on applications, approvals and processing stages.

In FY 2025-26, 645514 education loan applications were received on the portal across all education schemes. Out of these, 110667 applications were for PM-Vidyalaxmi loans.

In FY 2025-26, 110667 education loan applications were received under PM-Vidyalaxmi. Out of these, 70852 loans were sanctioned and 67728 loans have already been disbursed.

Gender Inclusion

PM-Vidyalaxmi ensures that all eligible meritorious students have access to financial support for higher education, regardless of their gender. Women and transgender students also stand to benefit from the scheme, making higher education more inclusive and accessible. By reducing financial barriers, the scheme helps students pursue quality education, improve their skills, and build better career prospects. This, in turn, increases their employability and encourages greater participation in the workforce, contributing to more inclusive social and economic development. In FY 2025-26, 368742 men and 276764 women applied for loans. 203438 loans were sanctioned for men and 158629 for women.

Empowering Underprivileged Students

The scheme facilitates the inclusion of students from financially weaker backgrounds into the mainstream education system, thereby enhancing overall inclusivity. Among the total applications submitted, there were students from the Economically Weaker Section (EWS), General category, Non-Creamy Layer Other Backward Classes (NCOBC), Other Backward Classes (OBC), Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and Persons with Disabilities (PwD). The involvement of applicants from all major social groups reflects the scheme’s extensive reach and inclusive framework. This underscores the scheme’s contribution to reducing financial barriers and promoting fair and equitable access to educational opportunities across different sections of society.

PM Vidyalaxmi Scheme: A Step Towards Educational Equity

The PM-Vidyalaxmi is a significant step towards expanding equitable access to higher education by providing collateral-free and guarantor-free education loans to meritorious students, complemented by targeted interest subvention for eligible families. By reducing financial barriers, the scheme enables greater participation in quality higher education, particularly for economically disadvantaged students. In doing so, it advances the objectives of the NEP 2020, contributes to the achievement of Sustainable Development Goal 4 on inclusive and equitable quality education, and supports the development of a skilled and future-ready human capital base for the country.

headline: Raksha Mantri virtually inaugurates Department of Military Medicine at Command Hospital (Central Command), Lucknow
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

Raksha Mantri virtually inaugurates Department of Military Medicine at Command Hospital (Central Command), Lucknow

The department, as R&D hub & Centre of Excellence, to equip the nation against emerging threats: Shri Rajnath Singh

RM calls for tech-driven preventive healthcare to enhance combat readiness

29 JUL 2026 1:23PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh virtually inaugurated the Department of Military Medicine at Command Hospital (Central Command) in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh on July 29, 2026. The inauguration marks the establishment of the country’s first dedicated academic and operational department exclusively focused on military medicine. The initiative aims to enhance combat medical readiness, advancing research, developing indigenous doctrines and creating specialised expertise for future battlefields & humanitarian contingencies. Established under the aegis of the Directorate General of Medical Services (Army), it marks a significant step in strengthening the operational medical preparedness of the Armed Forces Medical Services (AFMS).

In his address, Raksha Mantri emphasised that while economic and social development are essential aspects of nation-building, the fundamental basis of any nation’s sovereignty & progress lies in the strength and the morale of its military. He exuded confidence that the Department of Military Medicine would strengthen national security by ensuring advanced medical support for the troops, while reinforcing their confidence that they will receive care and support in times of need.

The Department will focus on key disciplines including Military Trauma and Damage Control; Combat Psychiatry & Resilience; Environmental & Operational Medicine; Military Medical Logistics; Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear & Explosive (CBRNe) Medical Response; Emergency Medicine & Critical Care; Disaster Medicine and Humanitarian Assistance & Disaster Relief (HADR) as well as Research, Audit & Data Analytics. It will also foster innovation in technology-enabled battlefield medicine, simulation-based training, telemedicine, prolonged field care and medical decision support.

The Department will be developed in a phased manner, with the initial phase focusing on establishment and commencement of academic programmes, followed by the creation of Centres of Excellence in HADR and CBRNe medicine, and eventual evolution into a nationally and internationally recognised centre for military medicine.

Highlighting the growing importance of military medicine, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that, just as aerospace medicine addresses the challenges faced by pilots and astronauts in low earth orbit, military medicine studies the physical and mental stresses exerted on the human body during war and war-like situations. “Our soldiers are deployed in some of the world’s most complex regions & harshest climates, exposed to diverse challenges. This new department will develop medical protocols tailored for these operational environments,” he said.

Raksha Mantri stressed that, alongside traditional weaponry, the threat of weapons of mass destruction persists in the current era. In such a situation, the department will serve as a hub for research and development, equipping the nation to deal with emerging threats arising out of the rapid technologies advancements, he said.

Shri Rajnath Singh underlined that, as the world’s largest democracy and a responsible power, India is one of the largest military contributors to United Nations peacekeeping missions, and the defence forces remain at the forefront of HADR operations far beyond national borders. This Department of Military Medicine will prove invaluable in enhancing expertise in disaster response, field hospital deployment, mass casualty management, and epidemic control.

This newly-established Department has been conceived as a centre of excellence in military medicine and will serve as the principal academic, research and doctrinal hub for AFMS. It will provide structured education and training in military and operational medicine, facilitate postgraduate programmes in domains such as combat medicine, combat surgery and trauma care, and promote indigenous research tailored to India's operational requirements.

Raksha Mantri expressed hope that the department will act as a training ground for young doctors of the Army Medical Corps in battlefield nursing and advanced trauma life support. “The department will open up a new career pathway for young medical professionals. Students will now be able to pursue super-specialisation in military medicine. This will not only enhance intellectual capital within the military, but also elevate India’s stature in medical research on the international stage,” he added.

Underscoring the critical need for ‘preventive healthcare’, Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that it should be viewed as the first line of defence, prior to actual treatment. He called for developing a system that can identify and mitigate a health risk at an early stage through disease surveillance, vaccination, sanitation, nutrition, physical fitness, occupational health, and regular health screenings. “Preventive healthcare is directly linked to combat readiness and national security. We can leverage technologies such as AI, wearable devices, predictive analytics, and advanced diagnostics to enhance real-time monitoring of soldiers’ health and the early identification of potential health risks,” he said.

Raksha Mantri concluded his address by describing the new Department of Military Medicine as a symbol of a revolutionary shift in the military mindset of the nation. “Together, we must transform this department into the world’s best ‘Battlefield Medicine Research Centre’,” he said.

The event was attended by Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth; Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh; Vice Chief of the Army Staff Lieutenant General Sandeep Jain; General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Central Command Lieutenant General Anindya Sengupta; DG AFMS Surgeon Vice Admiral Arti Sarin; Adjutant General Lieutenant General VPS Kaushik; and DG Medical Services (Army) & Colonel Commandant Army Medical Corps Lieutenant General CG Muralidharan; Additional Secretary, Department of Defence Shri Manish Tripathi; Commandant, Command Hospital (Central Command), Lucknow Major General Alok Bhalla, and other senior officials.

The establishment of the Department aligns with the Government’s vision of strengthening indigenous capabilities and enhancing the operational preparedness of the Defence Forces. It also complements the proposed Global Military Medicine Centre envisioned under the Raksha Strategy Vision 2026-30. The inauguration marks another significant milestone in the ongoing transformation of AFMS into a modern, technology-enabled, operationally relevant and patient-centric military healthcare system, while strengthening India's preparedness for future defence and national security challenges.

headline: Restoring Safety by Removing National Highway Encroachments
fullText:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways

Restoring Safety by Removing National Highway Encroachments

29 JUL 2026 12:38PM by PIB Delhi

India's National Highways are the backbone of the country's mobility and economic growth, carrying millions of commuters and transporting goods across states every day. However, one of the most persistent threats to road safety and efficient highway operations is unauthorised encroachment along highway corridors.

Illegal structures, commercial establishments, temporary sheds, roadside extensions, and other encroachments narrow carriageways, obstruct visibility, interfere with drainage systems, and create unsafe entry and exit points. Such obstructions significantly increase the risk of road crashes by forcing vehicles to make sudden lane changes, reducing reaction time, and distracting drivers. Encroachments also hamper highway maintenance, emergency response, and future infrastructure expansion.

Recognising the importance of keeping public roads safe and accessible, the Supreme Court has directed the removal of unauthorised encroachments on public roads and highways.

In line with this commitment, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) have been undertaking sustained anti-encroachment drives across the country. These operations are carried out in accordance with legal provisions and established procedures, with the objective of restoring the Right of Way (RoW), improving traffic movement, and enhancing safety for all road users.

One such initiative is being undertaken by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), PIU Rajkot, which has launched a large-scale anti-encroachment drive in strict compliance with the directives of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Suo Motu Writ Petition (Civil) No. 9 of 2025.

NHAI surveyed nearly 693 km of National Highways under its jurisdiction and issued 1,403 notices against unauthorised structures, illegal commercial accesses, and unapproved median cuts—major safety hazards that increase the risk of fatal crashes on high-speed corridors. Acting promptly, the authority has already removed more than 361 illegal accesses and encroachments and permanently closed 150 unauthorised median gaps. The drive has been carried out in close coordination with the respective District Magistrates (DMs) and Superintendents of Police (SPs), ensuring smooth and effective enforcement. Recent mega-drives have successfully cleared hundreds of unauthorised occupations along the religiously significant Somnath–Dwarka Highway, notably in Bardiya and the stretch from Honest Hotel to Hathi Chowk.

These initiatives are not merely enforcement exercises—they are road safety interventions. Every encroachment removed helps restore visibility, improves traffic flow, provides space for emergency operations, and reduces the likelihood of crashes. At the same time, protecting the designated Right of Way safeguards public investment in national infrastructure and enables future highway development without avoidable delays.
