headline: Tiger numbers and Tiger Reserves saw remarkable increase under PM Narendra Modi’s visionary leadership in last 12 years: Shri Bhupender Yadav
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Tiger numbers and Tiger Reserves saw remarkable increase under PM Narendra Modi’s visionary leadership in last 12 years: Shri Bhupender Yadav

Union Environment Minister addresses Global Tiger Day event in New Delhi, encourages People to respect Nature

Wildlife Conservation stories go beyond Bare Data; they assimilate Traditional Knowledge, Emotions, Passion and years of Experience: Shri Yadav

NTCA Eco-tourism webpage launched on Global Tiger Day 2026; NTCA Awards honour exemplary contributions to Tiger Conservation and Protected Area Management

29 JUL 2026 12:21PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today addressed the Global Tiger Day 2026 celebrations organised by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) in New Delhi. The Minister called for a deeper societal connect with nature and a conservation-oriented lifestyle. The event was graced by the presence of Union MoS (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, besides senior government officials, wildlife experts, frontline forest personnel, students and other stakeholders to celebrate India’s achievements in tiger conservation and reaffirm the collective commitment towards protecting tigers and their habitats.

Emphasising that conservation is not merely about protecting wildlife but also about developing a respectful relationship with nature, Shri Yadav said, “Nature is not only a source of tourism or entertainment, it also needs to be respected and people must derive peace from it.” He encouraged people to draw inspiration from nature and lead a lifestyle dedicated to environmental conservation.

Highlighting India’s conservation achievements, the Minister said that the number of tigers (3682) and tiger reserves (58) has seen a remarkable increase under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He added that the number of elephant reserves, national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, protected areas, community reserves and wetlands has also increased during the last 12 years.

While launching the NTCA Eco-tourism webpage, Shri Yadav congratulated NTCA for bringing information relating to all Tiger Reserves on an integrated platform. It provides direct links to authentic websites of all Tiger Reserves for safari and accommodation bookings, making information more accessible while promoting responsible and sustainable nature-based tourism. (Link: https://ntca.gov.in/eco-tourism/)

Speaking about the importance of documenting conservation experience, the Minister said, “The stories of forests is not bare data but it includes traditional knowledge, emotions, passion towards Wildlife Conservation and years long experiences of wildlife officers, Conservationists etc.” He urged forest officers to write more about wildlife conservation and share their experiences in a manner that can contribute to practical and implementable policy solutions.

Shri Yadav also stressed the need for capacity building of the forest officers and staff by incorporating global best practices. He highlighted the role of the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) in taking knowledge sharing to the world under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.

Recognising the contribution of those working on the ground for tiger conservation, NTCA Awards were presented to wildlife officers and other contributors for exemplary work in tiger conservation and protected area management. The celebrations also provided a platform to acknowledge the contribution of frontline personnel whose efforts are central to wildlife conservation.

The Minister also reviewed an exhibition showcasing the best entries from the painting, sketching, slogan-writing and mask-making competitions organised on the theme ‘Save Tiger’ for school children across Delhi-NCR. Further, a nationwide tiger conservation awareness campaign was also organised through Eco-clubs under the Ministry's Environment Education Programme, with special focus on schools located near Tiger Reserves.

Five publications were released during the celebrations, reflecting NTCA’s continued emphasis on science-based conservation, knowledge sharing and public awareness. These include the July 2026 edition of NTCA Outreach Journal – STRIPES; the Security Audit Report of 24 Tiger Reserves; a report on habitat suitability assessment for Sloth Bears across Tiger Landscapes in India; Tigers of the World, published by IBCA and GTF; and The Rehman Khera Tiger, by Shri Chandra Prakash Goyal and Shri Satya Prakash Yadav.

The Global Tiger Day 2026 celebrations reaffirmed India’s enduring commitment to tiger conservation through recognition of excellence, scientific management, capacity building, responsible eco-tourism, knowledge sharing and greater public participation in safeguarding the country’s rich natural heritage.

Background: Global Tiger Day 2026

A century ago, an estimated 1,00,000 wild tigers roamed across Asia. Today, they occupy less than 8% of their historic range, and three subspecies—the Bali, Javan, and Caspian tigers—have become extinct. The decline in tiger populations has been driven by poaching, illegal wildlife trade, habitat loss and fragmentation, human-wildlife conflict, and climate change.

Recognising the urgent need for collective action, the leaders of the 13 Tiger Range Countries came together at the St. Petersburg Tiger Summit in 2010 and launched the Global Tiger Recovery Program (GTRP). The Summit also established Global Tiger Day, to be observed annually on 29th July, with the ambitious TX2 goal of doubling the global wild tiger population by 2022.

Since then, Global Tiger Day has served as a global platform to raise awareness about tiger conservation, strengthen international cooperation, encourage public participation, and review progress in protecting tigers and their habitats.

headline: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: LONG RANGE FORECAST SYSTEM
fullText:
Ministry of Earth Sciences

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: LONG RANGE FORECAST SYSTEM

29 JUL 2026 11:49AM by PIB Delhi

Since 2021, the India Meteorological Department (IMD), under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), has adopted an advanced Multi-Model Ensemble (MME) approach for long-range forecasting. This has significantly improved the accuracy of long-range forecasts, with all forecasts issued since then remaining within the error limits. For example, operational monsoon forecasts since 2021 have been within the forecast error limits, with an average absolute error of 2.2% of the Long Period Average (LPA) over the five years (2021-2025). The year-wise details of the accuracy achieved by the IMD's Long-Range Forecast system during the last ten years are provided in the table below:

2024 | 108 | 106 | 106

2025 | 108 | 105 | 106

During the last ten years, the forecast error exceeded 10% of the LPA only once, in 2019, when the absolute forecast error was 14% of the LPA. Since the adoption of the MME strategy in 2021, the India Meteorological Department has significantly improved the accuracy of its long-range forecasts, achieving a mean absolute forecast error of only 2.2% of the LPA.

The India Meteorological Department, under the Ministry, has progressively upgraded its LRF system by adopting an advanced MME forecasting approach based on coupled dynamical climate models. The MME system combines forecasts from multiple climate models, thereby reducing uncertainties associated with individual models and improving the reliability and skill of seasonal forecasts. The adoption of the MME forecasting system has led to a significant improvement in the reliability of seasonal monsoon forecasts. During the period 2021–2025, the average absolute error of the first-stage forecast was 3.1% of the LPA, while the average absolute error of the second-stage forecast further reduced to 2.2% of the LPA. In comparison, the average absolute error during 2016–2020 was 7.8% of the LPA. Thus, the average absolute error has reduced from 7.8% to 2.2% of the LPA, indicating a substantial enhancement in the reliability and skill of the seasonal prediction system following the adoption and operational refinement of the MME forecasting system. The MME system has also enhanced the consistency of forecasts by improving the representation of large-scale climate drivers such as the El Nino–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), leading to more reliable seasonal monsoon predictions.

The Government has taken several measures to further improve long-range monsoon forecasting and prediction of extreme weather events in the country. These include:

Adoption of an advanced Multi-Model Ensemble and coupled dynamical climate models for operational long-range forecasting.

Continuous upgradation of numerical weather prediction models through improved model physics, higher spatial resolution, advanced data assimilation techniques, and enhanced computational capabilities.

Capacity enhancement under the Mission Mausam focuses on the modernization of meteorological observation systems through the expansion of the national observation network with additional Doppler Weather Radars (DWRs), Automatic Weather Stations (AWSs), Automatic Rain Gauges (ARGs), upper-air observing systems, wind profilers, and other observing platforms, along with the use of high-performance computing infrastructure and artificial intelligence/machine learning-based forecasting tools.

Expansion of satellite-based observations through indigenous meteorological satellites and the assimilation of satellite, radar, and in-situ observations into numerical models to improve forecast accuracy.

Dissemination of weather forecasts and warnings through multiple communication platforms, including mobile applications, APIs, web portals, SMS, television, radio, and social media, in coordination with Central and State Government agencies.

The above measures are being implemented uniformly across the country for the benefit of all States and Union Territories. Therefore, no State-wise allocation or distribution of these measures is maintained.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

headline: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: EXPANSION OF OCEAN OBSERVATION NETWORK
fullText:
Ministry of Earth Sciences

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: EXPANSION OF OCEAN OBSERVATION NETWORK

29 JUL 2026 11:47AM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has significantly strengthened the national ocean observation network. The details follow:

Ocean observation moorings: 19 subsurface moorings (16 in the mainland Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and 3 in the equatorial Indian Ocean) for monitoring ocean currents and zooplankton biomass, providing critical data for ocean model validation.

Tsunami monitoring network: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning System comprises 17 broadband seismic stations, 7 deep-ocean tsunami buoys, and 36 coastal tide gauges, along with 35 Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receivers and strong-motion accelerometers.

Coastal observation systems: The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) maintains a network of 17 Directional Wave Rider Buoys, 20 Acoustic Doppler Current Profilers (ADCPs), 32 Automatic Weather Stations (AWS), 2 Water Quality Buoys, and 50 tide gauges for continuous monitoring of coastal and ocean conditions.

Deep-sea and autonomous observations: INCOIS has deployed 302 Argo profiling floats (2014–2025), 12 deep-sea glider missions, 45 drifting buoys, 64 wave drifters, and advanced ocean observation instruments such as, Vertical Microstructure Profilers (VMPs), Underway Conductivity–Temperature–Depth (uCTD) systems, and Wire Walker systems.

The strengthened ocean observation network has significantly improved the accuracy of monsoon prediction, cyclone forecasting, and ocean-state forecasts by providing high-quality real-time observations for numerical weather and ocean models. Data from Argo profiling floats, moored buoys, tide gauges, and other ocean observing platforms are received at the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) through the Global Telecommunication System (GTS), quality-controlled, and assimilated into numerical models to generate accurate initial ocean conditions. This data assimilation reduces forecast errors and enhances the reliability of monsoon and cyclone predictions as well as ocean-state forecasts. The real-time wave observations from these buoys are utilized by INCOIS for operational wave forecasting and coastal early warning services.

The Government is continuously expanding and strengthening the national ocean observation network. Recent initiatives include installing 14 additional tide gauges and 15 co-located Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receivers to enhance tsunami monitoring and coastal observations. A Directional Wave Rider Buoy has also been deployed off Mauritius to improve the prediction of Southern Ocean swells affecting the north Indian coastal waters. Further, regular pre- and post-monsoon research vessel cruises have been institutionalized for deployment and maintenance of ocean observation systems, while collaboration with the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research – National Institute of Oceanography (CSIR–NIO), National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR) and other partner institutions has been strengthened to ensure sustained operation and expansion of the observation network.

Assimilation of real-time observation of data from the network has improved wave forecast accuracy by about 43% compared to 2014, with sustained forecast improvements during the five-day forecast period. The enhanced observation network has also enabled coastal forecast systems with an accuracy of about 70%. In addition, observations from tsunami buoys, tide gauges, GNSS receivers, and strong-motion accelerometers enable INCOIS to issue tsunami advisories within the stipulated 10-minute window following a tsunamigenic earthquake as per International Standards. The data from ocean observation platforms received in real time at the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) are assimilated into the INCOIS Global Ocean Data Assimilation System (INCOIS-GODS), which provides initial ocean conditions for the Coupled Forecast System (CFS) used for seasonal and extended-range forecasts, and the Hybrid Coordinate Ocean Model (HYCOM), which provides initial ocean conditions for the Hurricane Weather Research and Forecasting (HWRF) model used by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) for cyclone prediction. These systems substantially improve the country's monsoon and cyclone forecasting capabilities.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

headline: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: NCCR Studies on Microplastic Pollution
fullText:
Ministry of Earth Sciences

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: NCCR Studies on Microplastic Pollution

29 JUL 2026 11:45AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Earth Sciences, through the National Centre for Coastal Research (NCCR), monitors microplastics, mesoplastics, macroplastics and marine litter at selected locations along the Indian coast, including Thoothukudi and the Gulf of Mannar. The studies indicate that synthetic filaments are the predominant type of microplastic, while riverine discharge and Abandoned, Lost or Discarded Fishing Gear (ALDFG) are the major sources of microplastic pollution.

NCCR has developed a Clean Coast Index (CCI) based on the abundance of microplastics and macroplastics data available in the coastal environment. The CCI assessment classifies the Thoothukudi coast and the Gulf of Mannar as 'moderately clean'. The microplastic abundance in sediment is observed between 28 to 60 particles/50gm of the sediment along Gulf of Mannar and Thoothukudi coast. Based on the available information, no major microplastic pollution hotspots have been identified in the region.

The National Centre for Coastal Research (NCCR) undertakes scientific monitoring and assessment of marine litter and microplastics along the Indian coast and provides scientific inputs to the concerned Ministries and stakeholders for policy formulation and management.

The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) has undertaken several policy measures to reduce plastic pollution, including the prohibition of identified Single-Use Plastic (SUP) items having low utility and high littering potential with effect from 1 July 2022. MoEFCC has also notified the Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2022, introducing Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) Guidelines for plastic packaging. These guidelines prescribe mandatory targets for collection, recycling, reuse of rigid plastic packaging and use of recycled plastic content, thereby promoting sustainable plastic waste management and reducing the plastic footprint. Since 2022, about 232 lakh tonnes of plastic packaging waste have been processed under the EPR framework.

The draft National Marine Litter Policy has been prepared and has been shared with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) for consultation.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

headline: NIPUN Bharat Mission and Foundational Literacy and Numeracy
fullText:
Ministry of Education

NIPUN Bharat Mission and Foundational Literacy and Numeracy

29 JUL 2026 7:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of School Education & Literacy (DoSE&L), Ministry of Education (MoE) has launched a National Mission called “National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy (NIPUN Bharat Mission (NBM))” on 5th July, 2021 for ensuring that every child in the country necessarily attains foundational literacy and numeracy (FLN) by the end of Grade 2.

This Mission aligned with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, has been set up under the aegis of the centrally sponsored scheme of Samagra Shiksha - an integrated scheme for School Education. All States/Union Territories are implementing NBM. It is the first time that the age group of 3-6 years has been included in the school continuum in the foundational stage in 5+3+3+4 structure consisting of 3 years of Balvatika and Grades 1 & 2. The state-wise enrolment for Foundational Stage in Government and Government aided schools are at Annexure I.

Financial assistance is provided to States and UTs for implementation of the interventions under Samagra Shiksha including NBM as per the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWP&B) under Samagra Shiksha prepared by the States and UTs based on their requirements and priority. These plans are then appraised and approved/estimated by Project Approval Board (PAB) in consultation with the States and UTs as per the programmatic and financial norms of the scheme.

The funds are released for Samagra Shiksha as a whole, based on the fulfilment of certain conditions such as pace of expenditure, receipt of commensurate state share, audited accounts, statement on cumulative state share, statement on outstanding advances, up-to-date expenditure statement, and audited utilization certificate. The state-wise details of the funds allocated (as part of Samagra Shiksha) under NIPUN Bharat Mission during the last three years and the current year are at Annexure II.

The various initiatives undertaken under the NIPUN Bharat Mission to achieve universal Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) and improve learning outcomes include:-

A 3-month play based ‘School Preparation Module and Guidelines’ for Grade I named ‘Vidya Pravesh’ was launched on 29 July 2021. The goal of Vidya Pravesh programme is to promote school preparedness in all children coming to Grade- I from diverse backgrounds (Balvatika, Anganwadi Centers (AWCs), at home, private play schools etc.), to ensure a smooth transition of children to Grade-I. It provides play based, age and developmentally appropriate learning experiences in a joyful and stimulating environment leading to holistic development to bolster a child’s pre-literacy, pre-numeracy, cognitive and social skills. This Programme is being implemented across the country. From 2022-23 till date, more than 5 crore students in 8.8 lakh schools have been benefitted.

Jaadui Pitara (JP), a collection of Learning Teaching Material (LTM) for 3 to 6 years age group was launched on 20th February, 2023. It is a box having 53 LTM for the foundational stage like toys, games, puzzles, puppets, posters, flashcards, story cards, play book set for students, and handbooks for teachers. The user manual and all the activity cards, picture reading posters, story cards, and instructions of JP have been translated into 22 languages. It also consists of a Trainer’s Handbook ‘Unmukh’ which is a comprehensive guide for the trainers which has an activity bank for 3–6-year-old children.

The e-JaaduiPitara (e-JP) based on JP was launched on 10th February 2024. The e-JP is a mobile based application and website with play-based pedagogy and a way to disseminate the learning of Jaadui Pitara, (a collection of Play Based Learning Teaching Material (LTM) for 3 to 8 years age group). The browser can be accessed at https://ejaaduipitara.ncert.gov.in/.

Play and activity-based textbooks for classes 1 and 2 have also been prepared and shared with States/UTs (Hindi- “Sarangi”, English-“Mridang”, “Mathematics- Joyful-Mathematics and Anandmay-Ganit” and Urdu-“Shahnai”) fulfilling NEP 2020 and NCF-FS (National Curricular Framework for Foundational Stage) recommendations.

Primers have been developed in 121 local languages for FLN learning in mother tongue. These are languages spoken by at least 10,000 population.

Lakshya or Targets for Foundational Literacy and Numeracy starting from the Balvatika up to Grade 2 based on the learning outcomes have been developed on the basis of national and international research.

To ensure continuous professional development of teachers, the Government launched NISHTHA Online on the DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing) platform in October, 2020. The programme provides multilingual training modules, including text and video content aligned with the developmental goals and learning outcomes of Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN). DIKSHA also hosts a dedicated FLN vertical with high-quality learning resources accessible across the country, including socio-economically disadvantaged districts. Currently, DIKSHA hosts content in 133 languages (126 Indian languages and 7 foreign languages), and under NISHTHA FLN and ECCE, more than 15.57 lakh users have successfully completed the online training programme.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

headline: Implementation of PM SHRI scheme
fullText:
Ministry of Education

Implementation of PM SHRI scheme

29 JUL 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi

The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 emphasises the importance of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its role in school education. Under Para 4.24, the Policy envisages concerted curricular and pedagogical initiatives, including the introduction of contemporary subjects such as Artificial Intelligence at relevant stages to develop essential skills among students at all levels. In alignment with the vision of NEP 2020, which emphasises the integration of emerging technologies in education, including Artificial Intelligence, the Ministry of Education has undertaken several initiatives to equip teachers, school heads and teacher educators with the necessary competencies for AI-assisted pedagogy.

Strengthening of teacher education and continuous professional development is supported under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha, aligned with NEP 2020. The Scheme provides support for strengthening the physical infrastructure of Teacher Education Institutions (TEIs), including State Councils of Educational Research and Training (SCERTs) and District Institutes of Education and Training (DIETs); strengthening the academic and professional capacities of teacher educators; providing continuous academic support through Block Resource Centres (BRCs) and Cluster Resource Centres (CRCs); and supporting inservice training of teachers, school heads, teacher educators, resource persons, master trainers and newly recruited teachers through the approved Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWP&B) of the respective States/UTs. Further, the Ministry implements Information and Communication Technology (ICT) and digital initiatives under Samagra Shiksha to strengthen digital learning in Government schools by supporting digital infrastructure, digital boards, virtual classrooms, training resources and other emerging technologies.

The Department also implements NISHTHA (National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement), a flagship teacher capacity-building programme under Samagra Shiksha. The programme includes dedicated modules on AI in Education, digital pedagogy and educational technology. Subject-specific Level-II Educational Technology modules include digital tools for Mathematics, Science, Languages and Social Sciences. NISHTHA is delivered through the DIKSHA platform, enabling teachers to access self-paced digital learning resources.

Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA), the Nation's digital platform for school education, provides quality digital content, QR-coded Energised Textbooks (ETBs), teacher training resources and digital learning materials for States/UTs. DIKSHA has evolved into a robust Learning Management System (LMS) supporting end-to-end digital learning through course creation, content delivery, learner engagement, assessments, progress tracking and certification. The platform incorporates personalised and AI-enabled learning support and currently hosts more than 350 live courses, including about 59 courses on Artificial Intelligence and Digital Learning, thereby supporting continuous professional development of teachers and promoting AI-enabled teaching-learning practices.

To ensure that educators remain abreast of emerging technologies, the Ministry of Education and NCERT organise regular capacity-building programmes, consultation workshops and webinars covering Artificial Intelligence, Content-Pedagogy-Technology integration, Information and Communication Technology (ICT), Open Educational Resources and AI-enabled teaching-learning practices. Recognising the critical role of teachers in leveraging technology to improve learning outcomes, NCERT has been continuously organising AI-related training programmes, benefiting more than 96,000 participants. Further, NCERT regularly conducts AI Awareness, Ethical Usage and AI Tools training programmes. CBSE and NCERT also offer self-paced online courses on Artificial Intelligence. AI capacity building programmes for teachers are also organised by Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS) and Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS) through reputed institutions.

Further, under the National Mission for Mentoring (NMM), envisaged under Para 15.11 of NEP 2020, AI in Education has been identified as a dedicated sub-domain under the Digital Literacy domain to enable teachers to receive focused mentoring on the pedagogical and ethical use of Artificial Intelligence in classrooms.

The National Programme on Artificial Intelligence (NPAI) Skilling Framework recognises Artificial Intelligence as a compute-intensive domain requiring robust digital infrastructure, access to high-performance computing resources and a conducive ecosystem for research and innovation. In this context, the IndiaAI Mission aims to facilitate access to quality datasets for AI research and innovation, develop a skilled AI talent pool, make AI compute and critical infrastructure widely accessible, promote core and applied AI research across sectors, support scaling of AI-based solutions, and establish governance mechanisms for the responsible, ethical and trustworthy development and deployment of Artificial Intelligence.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Education Shri Jayant Chaudhary, in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

headline: Promotion of Mother Tongue-based Education
fullText:
Ministry of Education

Promotion of Mother Tongue-based Education

29 JUL 2026 7:08PM by PIB Delhi

Article 350 A of Indian Constitution states that “It shall be the endeavour of every State and of every local authority within the State to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother-tongue at the primary stage of education to children belonging to linguistic minority groups.

The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 at para 4.11, inter-alia, provides that it is well understood that young children learn and grasp nontrivial concepts more quickly in their home language/mother tongue. Home language is usually the same language as the mother tongue or that which is spoken by local communities. Wherever possible, the medium of instruction until at least Grade 5, but preferably till Grade 8 and beyond, will be the home language/mother tongue/local language/regional language. Thereafter, the home/local language shall continue to be taught as a language wherever possible. This will be followed by both public and private schools. High-quality textbooks, including in science, will be made available in home languages/mother tongue. In cases where home language/mother tongue textbook material is not available, the language of transaction between teachers and students will still remain the home language/mother tongue wherever possible. Teachers will be encouraged to use a bilingual approach, including bilingual teaching-learning materials, with those students whose home language may be different from the medium of instruction. All languages will be taught with high quality to all students.

Section 29(2)(f) of Right to Education Act, 2009 provides that “medium of instructions shall, as far as practicable, be in child’s mother tongue”.

As a follow-up to the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020, the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) has developed the National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCF-SE), 2023, in line with the vision and recommendations of the Policy. Subsequently, pursuant to the NCF-SE 2023, NCERT has developed and introduced new textbooks for Grades 1 to 9. In order to provide support to the States/UTs for promoting multilingual education, NCERT has translated textbooks for Grades 1, 2, 3, and 6 into all 22 Scheduled Languages, and these have been made digitally available. Further, of the 460 textbooks for Grades 4, 5, 7, and 8, a total of 368 have already been translated and made available digitally.

NCERT has been providing academic support and training to states, Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS), Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS), Army Welfare Education Society (AWES) and other school system regarding curriculum development, teacher training on new textbooks & digital technology, TLM, pedagogy and holistic assessment.

NCERT has developed teaching-learning material for Language Education including textbooks mapped with Curricular Goals, Competencies and Learning Outcomes as given in NCF-SE 2023 to facilitate the process of teaching learning and assessment in Indian Languages. For Balvatika 1, 2 & 3, NCERT has developed teaching -learning material viz. Jaadui Pitara and e-Jaadui Pitara, which are available in different languages.

In line with the NEP, 2020 and the National Curriculum Framework for Foundational Stage (NCF-FS) 2022, NCERT has developed foundational learning resources such as Anand (Balvatika Activity Book) and Unmukh (Teacher Trainer's Handbook), in 22 Scheduled Indian Languages.

Further, in order to promote multilingual education and preserve India's linguistic diversity, in line with the NEP 2020, NCERT has undertaken following initiatives with support of technology-enabled solutions especially in translation of curricular resources by the use and integration of technology and AI:

i. Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA) is the national digital platform for school education, providing high-quality digital learning resources and QR-coded Energised Textbooks (ETBs) across all grades under the vision of "One Nation, One Digital Platform." DIKSHA is adopted by all the 36 States and Union Territories, as well as central autonomous bodies and school education boards, including Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) and National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS). DIKSHA can be accessed by learners and teachers across the country and currently supports 135 languages, 128 Indian languages and 7 foreign languages.

ii. National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement (NISHTHA): The Ministry of Education has launched NISHTHA, a large-scale holistic programme to enhance the professional competencies of teachers and school leaders across the country with a view to improving the overall quality of school education. The programme is implemented across all States and Union Territories through face-to-face, online and blended modes of training. The online courses are hosted on the DIKSHA platform and are available in 11 Indian languages, depending on the programme.

iii. Development of Primers in Indian Languages: In collaboration with Central University of Odisha, Koraput, Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL), Mysuru, NCERT has developed primers for foundational literacy in scheduled and non-scheduled Indian languages. A total of 121 primers have been launched by the Ministry of Education and are available on NCERT Website and DIKSHA.

iv. Translation of Educational Modules: NCERT has translated Navchetna, New Criminal Laws, Chandrayan modules into several Indian languages using AI-enabled translation technologies, making them widely accessible through digital platforms.

V. Bhasha Sangam on DIKSHA: A dedicated Bhasha Sangam page on DIKSHA, provides multilingual learning resources in the form of videos and basic conversational phrases for learning-teaching in 22 scheduled Indian languages.

vi. Promotion of Bharatiya Bhasha Utsav: A nationwide 75-day Bharatiya Bhasha Utsav was conducted from September to December 2023 to encourage language learning and cultural integration through the use of regional languages and technology.

vii. Bhartiya Bhasha Summer Camp: Bhartiya Bhasha Summer Camp is being organized under the aegis of Ministry of Education from last two years and promotion of Multilingual education is being done in 22 scheduled Indian languages. In this event, participation of students, teachers and community in large numbers has been recorded.

These initiatives reflect the commitment of GoI/NCERT to ensuring equitable access to quality education in learners' native languages while leveraging technology and AI to scale multilingual educational content across the country.

Further, since Education is a subject under the Concurrent List of the Constitution, the respective State/Union Territory (UT) Governments and its agencies may develop suitable curriculum in regional languages as per the local needs and demands, in accordance with the spirit and recommendations of the NEP, 2020.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Education Shri Jayant Chaudhary, in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

fullText:
Ministry of Education

Vacancies in Central Educational Institutions

29 JUL 2026 7:08PM by PIB Delhi

Occurring of vacancies in Central Educational Institutions and filling thereof is a continuous process. The vacancies arise due to promotion, retirement, resignation, death, opening of new institutions, schemes or projects, and additional requirements on account of enhanced students’ strength and expansion of capacity in existing institutions.

Education being a subject of Concurrent List of the Constitution, an overwhelming majority of the schools in the country come under the administrative control of the concerned State Governments/ Union Territory administrations.

In August, 2021, all the Central Higher Educational Institutions (CHEIs) under the Ministry of Education were requested to undertake a special drive to fill backlog vacancies in their institutions in Mission Mode. The CHEIs undertook special recruitment drives to fill the vacancies including Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs). In September 2022, the Ministry of Education had also exhorted all the CHEIs to fill up the vacancies in Mission Mode. In October 2025, all the CHEIs have again been requested to fill up all the backlog vacancies in Mission Mode. From September 2022, all CHEIs have undertaken Mission Mode recruitment drives to fill the vacancies. Up to 23.05.2026 (i.e. the date of the last Rozgar Mela), a total number of 32,114 posts have been filled up by all CHEIs, including 18,757 faculty positions, in Mission Mode.

The implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 is a continuous and ongoing process. Various autonomous organizations under the Ministry of Education are implementing the provisions of the Policy in a phased manner and regularly assessing the progress achieved.

NEP 2020 accords priority to strengthen physical infrastructure, particularly in rural and remote areas, through the construction of new buildings, addition of classrooms, upgrading of facilities, provision of barrier-free access for children with special needs, and improved sanitation and hygiene. Samagra Shiksha, PM-SHRI (Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India) and PM-USHA (Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan) are amongst many initiatives contributing to building a safe and inclusive infrastructure and learning environment. Similarly, initiatives like PM-Poshan and PM-Vidyalakshmi provide nutrition and financial assistance to students to access education and aim to ensure retention.

Significant progress has been achieved through the adoption of DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure of Knowledge Sharing) by all 36 States/UTs and autonomous bodies, the operation of 200 PM eVIDYA DTH TV channels and radio services, large-scale capacity building of teachers under NISHTHA (National Initiative for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement), expansion of inclusive digital education through Indian Sign Language content, PRASHAST 2.0 and accessible learning resources, and strengthening of digital infrastructure and technology-enabled learning under the ICT (Information and Communication Technology) component of Samagra Shiksha. These initiatives are regularly reviewed to ensure effective implementation of the objectives of NEP 2020.

Samagra Shiksha aims to ensure that all children, from pre-school to class 12, have access to quality education. Under the scheme, financial assistance is provided to the States and UTs to strengthen the physical and technical infrastructure of the schools. The details of funds allocated and utilized under Samagra Shiksha during the last five years is as follows:

Digital learning has also been strengthened through the extensive use of platforms such as DIKSHA, PM eVIDYA, e-Pathshala, SATHEE (Self-Assessment, Test and Help for Entrance Exams), SWAYAM Plus (Study Webs of Active-learning for Young Aspiring Minds), SWAYAM MOOCs (Massive Open Online Courses), the NIOS (National Institute of Open Schooling) Portal, YouTube channels, PM eVIDYA DTH channels, Mukta Vidya Vani radio, TARA (Teacher’s Assistant for Reading Assessment) App, SAMAGAM Portal and PRASHAST (Pre-Assessment Holistic Screening Tool) App.

headline: Alignment of Academics with Employment Opportunities
fullText:
Ministry of Education

Alignment of Academics with Employment Opportunities

29 JUL 2026 7:07PM by PIB Delhi

The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 promotes holistic, multidisciplinary and flexible higher education, enabling students to acquire knowledge and skills beyond a single discipline and pursue diverse educational and professional pathways. It emphasizes the importance of industry-academic connect and promotes research and innovation by setting up start-up incubation centres; centres in frontier areas of research; greater industry-academic linkages; and interdisciplinary research including humanities and social sciences. The National Credit Framework (NCrF), National Higher Education Qualifications Framework (NHEQF), Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) and Multiple Entry and Multiple Exit provisions provide a framework for integration, accumulation and transfer of academic, vocational and experiential learning.

To strengthen the linkage between academic learning and job requirements, higher education curricula provide for outcome-based education, skill-based modules, project-based learning, internships and industry interaction. University Grants Commission (UGC) and All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) have issued Guidelines for Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programme (AEDP) to be offered by Higher Education Institutions and Technical Institutions to provide practical exposure during the course of study expected with the aim to enhance competences of the graduates and the employment thereof. UGC and AICTE follow an assessment process for the apprenticeship component involving industry/establishment, academia and HEIs.

National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) aims at providing on-the-job training and skilling of Indian youth. It is implemented by the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education through four regional Boards of Apprenticeship Training/Practical Training (BoATs/BoPT) located at Mumbai, Kanpur, Chennai and Kolkata. During the last five years (2021-2022 to 2025-2026) approximately 17.22 lakh apprentices have been engaged under NATS. During this period, the Ministry of Education released Rs 2892.75 crore towards stipend support to apprentices. The NATS 2.0 portal has been introduced as a technology-enabled platform for registration and management of apprenticeship training, including digital processing of apprenticeship contracts, monitoring of training and stipend-related processes and improved tracking of apprentices and establishments. Under NATS, till date ~457 MOUs have been signed with HEIs for AEDP implementation. Further more than 75,000 apprentices have benefited from the AI Apprenticeship Programme.

AICTE has undertaken a comprehensive evaluation of Technical Education curricula in most of the emerging areas and core engineering courses along with pedagogical practices to ensure alignment with evolving industry requirements. This evaluation has focused on shifting emphasis from degree-centric learning to skills, adaptability, hands-on exposure and industry relevance. Model curricula is developed in consultation with leading academicians (from institutes of national importance), industry experts, public organizations and research institutions. These curricula embed experiential learning, internships, multidisciplinary exposure and emerging technology competencies to meet current and future workforce needs. The model curriculum reduces credit requirements to allow for more flexibility and includes "Value-added" courses focused on employability. A key outcome of the evaluation is the requirement for mandatory internships (industrial/social) for students, providing direct exposure to real-world working environments. A dedicated portal connects students directly with industry partners for internship. AICTE has also launched Project PRACTICE in September 2025 that aims to shift focus from theoretical rote learning to hands-on project-based learning and industry-connected, skill-based training in AICTE approved institutions from tier-2/tier-3 cities. Further, AICTE has initiated several key reforms to integrate work-based learning, project portfolios and AI-relevant competencies into campus programmes. The key reforms include integration of emerging and AI-relevant technologies in curricula, inclusion of courses and electives on Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Robotics, Cyber-Physical Systems, in alignment with industry engagement.

The University Grant Commission (UGC) has supported skill-based education through Community Colleges, B.Voc. Degree Programmes and Deen Dayal Upadhyay Centres for Knowledge Acquisition and Upgradation of Skilled Human Abilities and Livelihood.

Employability skills modules have been included as a part of job roles/SWAYAM in the curriculum which include Communication Skills, Self-Management Skills, Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Skills, Entrepreneurship Skills and Green Skills. To support skill development, the SWAYAM Plus portal has also been launched, focusing on upskilling and reskilling the workforce. More than 500 courses have been developed curated from 89 industry partners across 17 sectors and offered in emerging areas such as AI, Data Analyst etc.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

headline: Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda Reviews Preparedness for NEET UG Counselling 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda Reviews Preparedness for NEET UG Counselling 2026

Reviews readiness of the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) for a seamless, transparent and technology-enabled counselling process

Student-friendly counselling reforms introduced; one-time physical reporting, online document verification and enhanced facilities for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities

Ensure Every Proactive Measure is Taken to Address Candidates' Concerns: Union Health Minister

29 JUL 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda today reviewed the preparedness for the forthcoming NEET UG Counselling 2026, reaffirming the Government's commitment to ensuring a transparent, merit-based, technology-enabled and student-friendly admission process for undergraduate medical courses across the country. The review assessed the preparedness for counselling of All India Quota (AIQ) and other seats under the purview of the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC), Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

During the review, the Minister assessed the preparedness of the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC), Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) and other stakeholders involved in the counselling process. He reviewed the counselling schedule, IT infrastructure, cybersecurity preparedness, grievance redressal mechanisms, candidate facilitation measures and coordination with participating institutions.

Shri Nadda emphasized that the counselling process must be conducted in a transparent, fair and merit-based manner while ensuring a seamless experience for students. He directed officials to maintain robust technical support, ensure prompt grievance redressal and facilitate the smooth functioning of the counselling portal throughout the admission process. He directed the officials to ensure that every proactive measure is taken to address candidates' concerns.

The Minister was informed that NEET UG Counselling 2026 introduces several major technology-enabled and student-centric reforms aimed at enhancing transparency, improving accessibility and simplifying the admission process.

One of the key reforms is the introduction of a one-time physical reporting framework, significantly reducing the need for repeated visits by candidates. Following seat allotment, candidates will be able to exercise their willingness online by selecting either the Freeze or Float option.

Candidates opting for the Freeze option will physically report to their allotted institute within the prescribed schedule to complete admission formalities, including verification of original documents and payment of the admission fee.

Candidates opting for the Float option for participating in subsequent rounds for upgradation will be able to complete admission formalities, including document verification, through the online mode within the stipulated timeline. During this period, they will not be required to physically report to the allotted institute, submit original documents or pay the admission fee. Their provisional admission will remain valid while participating in subsequent counselling rounds.

The upgradation facility will remain available up to the third round of counselling. After completion of the third round, candidates holding allotted seats will report physically to their respective institutions for verification of original documents, payment of admission fees and completion of institutional formalities.

The revised framework ensures one-time physical reporting, one-time verification of original documents and one-time payment of admission fees, thereby reducing unnecessary travel, simplifying admission procedures and providing greater convenience to students.

Another important reform introduced this year is the online resignation facility. Candidates wishing to resign from their allotted seat, wherever permitted under the applicable counselling rules and timelines, will now be able to submit their resignation through the MCC Counselling Portal without the need to physically visit the allotted institute, unless otherwise specified in the Information Bulletin or notified separately by MCC.

The review also highlighted several measures to strengthen transparency and operational efficiency, including pre-populated candidate data received from the National Testing Agency (NTA), online document verification, validation of the seat matrix by the National Medical Commission (NMC) and verification by participating institutes.

Special emphasis has been placed on improving accessibility for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD). To facilitate greater accessibility, transparency and uniformity in assessment, the number of designated assessment centres has been expanded from 16 to 61 across the country.

In accordance with the National Medical Commission Guidelines dated 27 July 2026, the certificate issued by designated Medical Boards will now be known as the "Eligibility Certificate", reflecting its purpose of determining a candidate's eligibility for admission to the MBBS course based on functional assessment. The revised guidelines establish a transparent, uniform, evidence-based and competency-oriented framework for assessment of PwBD candidates while ensuring equal opportunity, academic standards, professional competence and patient safety.

The new guidelines also provide for an Appellate Disability Assessment Board, enabling eligible candidates to appeal against the assessment of the initial Disability Assessment Board in accordance with the provisions of the Information Bulletin.

Another significant reform is the complete digitisation of the admission process under the NRI category. Registration for NRI candidates will now be conducted entirely through the online counselling portal in accordance with the prescribed eligibility criteria. Candidates will upload all required documents online, replacing the earlier practice of submission through email. The uploaded documents will be verified online by designated Document Verification Officers, ensuring a transparent, efficient and time-bound verification process. MCC though its public notice issued on 27th May, 2026 has already informed that the candidates applying under the NRI category will be required to submit evidentiary proof and relevant legal documents during the counselling process, in accordance with the directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, establishing that the sponsor is the bona fide legal guardian of the candidate under the provisions of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890.

Shri Nadda was also informed that cybersecurity preparedness has been comprehensively reviewed in coordination with the National Informatics Centre (NIC). Training programmes have been conducted for Disability Assessment Boards, college nodal officers and Document Verification Officers to ensure uniform implementation of the counselling process across the country.

To strengthen candidate support, a 24×7 toll-free call centre (1800-102-7637) has been established. Bilingual information material, frequently asked questions and guidance videos are also being made available through various platforms to assist candidates throughout the counselling process. A dedicated email-based grievance redressal mechanism (mcc2026[at]gov[dot]in) has also been established for prompt resolution of candidate queries.

The National Testing Agency declared the NEET (UG) 2026 results on 16 July 2026. The counselling process for All India Quota seats in MBBS, BDS and B.Sc. (Hons.) Nursing is expected to commence shortly.

Candidates have been advised to carefully read the Information Bulletin, counselling scheme and applicable rules before exercising options relating to seat acceptance, upgradation, resignation or disability assessment. They have also been advised to regularly visit the official MCC counselling portal and adhere to the notified counselling schedule throughout the admission process.

Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastva, Additional Secretary, Medical Education Smt. Vinod Kotwal, Director General of Health Services, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare Dr. Loveneesh G Krishna, Director General, National Informatics Centre Shri Priyank Bharti and other senior officials participated in the review meeting.

Panchayat Resource Persons Being Engaged as Nasha Mukti Mitras to Promote Drug-Free Villages

29 JUL 2026 6:38PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India is strengthening grassroots efforts to combat drug abuse under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan (NMBA) by promoting greater participation of Panchayati Raj Institutions in awareness generation and community mobilisation. The initiative aims to build a people-led movement against substance abuse by engaging local communities and volunteers at the village level.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B. L. Verma, in a written reply to Shri Harsh Mahajan in the Rajya Sabha today.

The Minister informed that while no separate scheme has been formulated for convergence of Panchayati Raj Institutions with the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) specifically for village-level drug awareness, all Panchayati Raj Departments of States and Union Territories, including Himachal Pradesh, have been requested under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan to identify and engage Panchayat Resource Persons as Nasha Mukti Mitras (NMMs).

These Nasha Mukti Mitras have been entrusted with promoting the NMBA Mass Pledge against drug abuse through both online and offline campaigns. They are also being integrated into existing awareness drives and are promoting the use of the NMBA logo, mascot and the National De-addiction Helpline 14446 to strengthen outreach at the grassroots level.

The Minister further informed that under the State Action Plan (SAP) component of the NAPDDR Scheme, financial assistance is provided to State Governments and Union Territory Administrations for preventive education, awareness generation, capacity building and drug demand reduction activities. During the last two financial years, no funds were released to Himachal Pradesh in 2023–24 and 2024–25. However, ₹1.34 crore was released to the State during 2025–26 to support activities under the State Action Plan.

The Government continues to strengthen the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan through active participation of Panchayati Raj Institutions, community volunteers, educational institutions and civil society organisations to create sustained awareness against drug abuse and realise the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has strengthened the monitoring and evaluation of de-addiction and rehabilitation centres supported under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) through a robust digital monitoring mechanism and periodic inspections. Assessments also examine staffing, quality of medical and psychosocial services, follow-up care, maintenance of records, utilization of funds, and outreach activities undertaken by the centres.

It records patient registration details, clinical assessments, substance use patterns, diagnosis, treatment, pharmacological and psychosocial interventions, and follow-up services. The system enables effective monitoring of treatment outcomes and rehabilitation of beneficiaries.

The Ministry also informed that de-addiction centres are regularly inspected by the Project Monitoring Unit through random surprise visits in accordance with the Standard Operating Procedure. Continuation of projects and release of grants are contingent upon satisfactory inspection reports. Centres found not functioning in accordance with the Scheme guidelines are liable for closure, ensuring accountability and quality standards in service delivery.

The Government remains committed to strengthening India's de-addiction ecosystem through transparent monitoring, digital governance, and quality rehabilitation services, contributing to the objectives of a healthier and drug-free society.

Government Expands Welfare and Empowerment Initiatives for SCs, OBCs, Senior Citizens and Persons with Disabilities in Tamil Nadu

Nearly 9.67 Lakh SC Students Receive Post-Matric Scholarships in 2025-26; Over 8.75 Lakh OBC Students Covered Under Pre-Matric Scholarship in 2024-25

29 JUL 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India continues to strengthen educational, economic and social empowerment of Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Senior Citizens and Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) in Tamil Nadu through a wide range of flagship schemes implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The Minister informed that under the Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Castes, the number of beneficiaries increased from 6,43,761 in 2023-24 to 9,34,793 in 2024-25 and further to 9,66,840 in 2025-26. Similarly, the Pre-Matric Scholarship for SCs and Others benefited 3,35,642 students in 2023-24, 5,21,124 students in 2024-25 and 5,82,684 students in 2025-26.

Under the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY), the number of beneficiaries increased from 507 in 2023-24 to 894 in 2024-25, while 666 beneficiaries were covered during 2025-26.

The SRESHTA scheme for residential education benefited 238 students in 2023-24, 312 students in 2024-25 and 267 students in 2025-26.

The reply further stated that the Ministry continued to support students belonging to OBCs, Economically Backward Classes (EBCs) and Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs). Under the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme, 2.94 lakh students in 2023-24, 8.75 lakh students in 2024-25 and 2.76 lakh students have been benefitted in 2025-26. The Minister further informed that welfare initiatives for senior citizens and economically weaker sections continued to benefit thousands of people in the State. An assessment carried out by the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO), NITI Aayog has observed that the Ministry's targeted interventions have contributed to notable improvements in access to education for marginalized communities. headline: Access to Quality Education
fullText:
Ministry of Education

Access to Quality Education

29 JUL 2026 6:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of School Education & Literacy is implementing an integrated scheme for school education - Samagra Shiksha, which covers the entire gamut from pre-school to class XII. The scheme is aligned with NEP 2020 to ensure that all children have access to quality education with an equitable and inclusive classroom environment which should take care of their diverse background, multilingual needs, different academic abilities and make them active participants in the learning process.

Under the scheme, financial assistance is provided to States and UTs for undertaking various activities for providing universal access to holistic and qualitative school education including opening/strengthening of new schools up to senior secondary level, construction of school buildings & additional classrooms, development/strengthening of school infrastructure in border areas under Vibrant Village Programme through the convergence of existing scheme of DOSEL, setting up, construction of hostels for PVTGs under PM-JANMAN, setting up of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Avasiya Vidyalayas, construction of hostels under Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan for unsaturated ST population, free uniforms to eligible children and free text books at elementary level, transport allowance and undertaking enrolment & retention drives. Special training for age-appropriate admission of out of school children and residential as well as non-residential training for older children, seasonal hostels / residential camps, special training centers at worksites, transport/ escort facility etc. are also supported to bring out of school children to the formal schooling system. Support is also provided for skill education, integrated science labs/maths.

PM eVidya unifies all efforts related to digital/online/on-air education to enable multi-mode access to education across the country under the aegis of National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. PM eVidya includes 200 DTH TV Channels and 400 Radio channels to provide supplementary education as per requirement in various Indian languages for classes 1-12.

Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI) is a centrally sponsored scheme which aims to strengthen more than 14,500 schools from amongst the existing schools managed by Central Government/State/UT Government/local bodies. These PM SHRI schools are to showcase all the initiatives of National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, be exemplar schools, and also offer benchmarking leadership to other schools in the neighbourhood.

Under the Scheme(s), annual plans are prepared by the respective States /UTs, including for rural and underserved areas, as per their priority and requirements. These annual plans are appraised and approved by the Project Approval Board (PAB) in the Department, in consultation with the respective State/UT, as per the programmatic and financial norms of the Scheme.

Accordingly, for 2026-27, under Samagra Shiksha, central share of Rs 722.93 crore has been approved for the State of Punjab and under PM SHRI, central share of Rs 140.10 crore for 356 PM SHRI Schools has been approved for the State of Punjab for providing qualitative and holistic education in the State.

Further, education is in the concurrent list of the Constitution and the majority of the schools are under the administrative control of the respective State/UT Government.

Inclusive Education component of Samagra Shiksha provides support to CwSN via specific student-oriented interventions such as identification and assessment camps, provision of aids, appliances and assistive devices, scribe, transportation and escort allowance support, Braille books and large print books, stipend for girls with special needs and teaching-learning materials etc. in order to appropriately address their unique educational requirements in general schools. Further, individualized support is also provided through therapeutic interventions at the block level. Samagra Shiksha also has provisions for creation of differently abled friendly infrastructure such as ramps with handrails and differently-abled friendly toilets for barrier free access in schools.

The Government of India is implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme called Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram, popularly known as ULLAS: Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society from 2022-23 to 2026-27. The scheme, aligned with NEP 2020 targets adults (aged 15 and above) who are not literate and focuses on rural areas, districts/blocks with large SC/ST/ population, educationally backward areas, women etc. The scheme is implemented in a hybrid mode, allowing States/UTs to adopt offline, online or blended approaches. The scheme is based on volunteerism to impart foundational literacy and numeracy. 9 States/ UTs (Ladakh, Mizoram, Tripura, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, A & N Islands, Chandigarh, Sikkim and Uttarakhand) have declared Full Literacy.

The Central Government provides financial assistance to States/UTs under the Centrally Sponsored scheme - Samagra Shiksha for strengthening of existing government schools, including, creation and augmentation of infrastructure facilities like buildings, toilets for Boys/Girls/CWSN, drinking water, electricity and digital facilities based on Annual Work Plan & Budget (AWP&B) proposal prepared by them and gaps determined from Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE) database. These plans are then appraised and approved by the Project Approval Board (PAB) in the Department of School Education and Literacy in consultation with the State/UT as per the programmatic and financial norms of the scheme, physical and financial progress of works sanctioned earlier and availability of budgetary resources.

The Department of School Education & Literacy, from time to time, through review meetings and PAB meetings, requests the State Governments and UT administrations to fill up infrastructure gaps.

This information was given by Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

Ministry of Education

Vacancies in Schools

29 JUL 2026 6:29PM by PIB Delhi

Education being a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution, the majority of schools in the country are under the administrative control of the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. Accordingly, the recruitment, service conditions and deployment of teachers fall within the administrative domain of the concerned States/UTs. Teacher vacancies arise from time to time due to factors such as retirement, resignation, creation of new posts, rationalisation of teacher deployment and changes in enrolment, including in rural, tribal and aspirational districts. The data relating to sanctioned strength, working strength and vacancies of teachers in Government schools at the primary, upper primary, secondary and senior secondary levels, State-wise, is maintained by the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations.

As per the UDISE+ 2025-26, the State/UT-wise details of teachers in position in Government schools across the country, are placed at Annexure-I.

Further, as per the UDISE+ 2025-26, the State/UT-wise details of single-teacher schools in the country, are placed at Annexure-II.

The Central Government periodically advises States/UTs to fill vacant posts through transparent and merit-based recruitment processes, including through autonomous teacher recruitment boards or similar mechanisms. The progress of recruitment is regularly reviewed through meetings and advisories, with emphasis on competitive selection, consistency and technology-based teacher requirement planning and forecasting.

Further, the Central Government provides financial assistance to States/UTs under Samagra Shiksha to maintain appropriate Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) at various levels of schooling in accordance with the norms prescribed under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.

Para 2.3 of the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 emphasises maintaining a PTR of under 30:1 in each school and under 25:1 in areas with a high proportion of socio-economically disadvantaged students. As per UDISE+ 2025-26 report, the PTR at the national level stands at 19 at Primary level, 17 at Upper Primary level, 15 at Secondary level, and 23 at the Higher Secondary level which is within the norms envisaged under NEP 2020.

Moreover, the Ministry of Education is implementing a National Mission to improve learning outcomes at the School Education level through an integrated teacher training programme called ‘National Initiative for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement’ (NISHTHA). NISHTHA courses have been designed and are run for Elementary, Secondary, Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN), Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) and Educational Technology and are offered online by NCERT on the DIKSHA platform using high-quality professionally made e-content.

headline: National Education Policy (NEP), 2020
fullText:
Ministry of Education

National Education Policy (NEP), 2020

29 JUL 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi

In line with the recommendations of the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020, skill-based and experiential learning has been promoted across school and higher education. Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha, skill education has been integrated as a regular component for students of Classes VI to XII. For Classes VI to VIII, exposure to skill education is provided through pre-vocational education, including 10 bagless days, a separate off-textbook experiential learning programme and Kaushal Bodh, the NCERT activity-based textbook series. For Classes IX to XII, skill courses aligned with the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF) are offered, with skill modules as an additional subject at the Secondary level and skill courses as an elective subject at the Senior Secondary level.

In higher education, skill-based education is supported through Community Colleges, B.Voc. Degree Programmes and Deen Dayal Upadhyay Centres for Knowledge Acquisition and Upgradation of Skilled Human Abilities and Livelihood. Further, UGC and AICTE have issued Guidelines for Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programme (AEDP), 2025 for higher education programmes under their respective domains. AEDP with National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS), provides opportunities to combine academic learning with structured apprenticeship and on-the-job training and industry exposure. Skill-based learning is also supported through programmes in emerging areas such as Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Cyber Security, Quantum Technology, Space Technology, Sustainable Energy, Internet of Things, Robotics and Semiconductors. These initiatives promote experiential, skill-based and industry-linked learning and support the development of employability and entrepreneurial abilities.

The Ministry of Education implements ICT and Digital initiatives such as PM eVidya and DIKSHA under Samagra Shiksha to enhance digital learning in Government schools across the country including the rural, remote and tribal areas. The initiatives aim to enhance the quality of education by integrating technology into teaching and learning processes. Under the scheme, funds are provided for setting up ICT Labs and Smart Classrooms according to the requirement of the State submitted in the Annual Work Plan & Budget (AWP&B).

A comprehensive initiative called PM eVidya was initiated as part of Atma Nirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan on 17th May, 2020, which unifies all efforts related to digital/online/on-air education to enable multi-mode access to education across the country. States/UTs collaborate with NCERT to utilise, monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of these initiatives as per their requirements. The key components of PM eVidya are also aligned towards enhancing digital literacy and include 200 DTH TV channels and 400 Radio channels to enable all States/UTs to provide supplementary education in various Indian languages for classes 1-12.

Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA) is the Nation’s One Nation, One Digital platform for providing quality e-content for school education in States/UTs along with QR coded Energised Textbooks (ETBs) for all grades. As a participant in DIKSHA, States/UTs/Autonomous Bodies (ABs) have generated and contributed over 3.67 lakh content in mother tongue/local/regional languages enabling multilingualism. Overall, 579.41 crore learning sessions for 2.29 crore users have been completed on DIKSHA by students, teachers and other stakeholders. The stakeholders also have access to more than 836 Virtual Labs on DIKSHA that help them with simulation of real-world laboratory environments. The platform supports both online and offline access, enabling learners to download content and continue learning without internet connectivity. These digital initiatives provide free curriculum aligned e-content to students, parents and teachers for supplementary academic resources.

The Government of India, in the Budget 2025, has announced provision of broadband connectivity to all Government Secondary schools in rural areas, under the ‘BharatNet’ project by BSNL to enhance digital infrastructure in remote areas in a phased manner.

To bridge the urban-rural education divide, Samagra Shiksha focuses on equal opportunities for schooling, equitable learning outcomes, bridging social and gender gaps and ensuring equity and inclusion in school education. The availability of digital learning platforms, smart classrooms and other technology-enabled learning resources provides access to educational content across different regions.

In higher education, digital learning platforms such as SWAYAM, SWAYAM Prabha, e-PG Pathshala and the UGC e-resource portal provide access to educational content and courses. The integration of the UGC e-resource portal with the Digital Seva Portal enables access to digital learning resources through Common Service Centres, including in rural areas. The UGC e-resource portal also provides selected digital content in regional languages. Further, the regulatory framework for Open and Distance Learning and Online Education provides for access to higher education through these modes while the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Programme includes faculty capacity-building through technology-enabled and ICT-based pedagogy. The Union Budget 2026–27 announced provision of Viability Gap Funding (VGF)/capital support for girls' hostels in Higher Education Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) institutions, covering every district. There was also an announcement in Budget 2025-2026 of Bhartiya Bhasha Pustak Yojana (BBPY) to provide digital-form Indian language books for school and higher education. These measures support access to education and digital learning opportunities across different regions.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Education Dr Sukanta Majumdar, in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

Ministry of Education

Posts and Vacancies in Higher Education

29 JUL 2026 6:24PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Higher Education Institutions (CHEIs) under Ministry of Education including Central Universities (CUs) and Centrally Funded Technical Institutions (CFTIs) such as Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), and National Institutes of Technology (NITs) are statutory autonomous organizations established under respective Central Acts of Parliament and governed by provisions of the Acts/Statutes/Ordinances/Regulations made thereunder. As autonomous institutions, faculty recruitment is done within the institutions itself, in accordance with their Acts and Regulations. The recruitment powers vests with the respective Board of Governors/Executive Committee/Board of Management.

Occurring of vacancies and filling thereof is a continuous process. The vacancies arise due to promotion, retirement, resignation, death, opening of new institutions, schemes or projects, and additional requirements on account of enhanced students’ strength and expansion of capacity in existing institutions.

In August, 2021, all CHEIs under the Ministry of Education were requested to undertake a special drive to fill backlog vacancies in their institutions in Mission Mode. The CHEIs undertook special recruitment drives to fill the vacancies including Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs). In September 2022, the Ministry of Education had also exhorted all the CHEIs to fill up the vacancies in Mission Mode. In October 2025, all the CHEIs have again been requested to fill up all the backlog vacancies in Mission Mode. From September 2022, all CHEIs have undertaken Mission Mode recruitment drive to fill the vacancies. Up to 23.05.2026 (i.e. the date of last Rozgar Mela), a total number of 32,114 posts (3,851 SC, 1,643 ST, 6,785 OBC, 1,191 EWS) have been filled up by all CHEIs, including 18,757 faculty positions (2,315 SC, 910 ST, 3,986 OBC, 568 EWS), in Mission Mode.

The number of PhD admissions at CHEIs is dynamic and varies across admission cycles based on the availability of faculty supervisors, departmental requirements, and funding support. Further, the availability of PhD positions changes with the Institute’s faculty strength. New faculty members create additional research supervision capacity, while the research scholars of faculty members who resign, retire, or are transferred are reassigned to other eligible supervisors as per the Institute’s academic regulations. The number of PhD enrolment has increased from 1,17,301 (as per AISHE Report 2014-15) to 3,43,559 (as per AISHE Report 2023-24) marking a growth of 192.89 %.

This information was given by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Education, Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.
